nodes.title: Finiteness of the nearly ordinary Hecke algebra over Λ′
nodes.statement: (Skinner–Wiles Corollary 3.4.) Let F have even degree. For every U, T_∞(U, 𝒪) is a finite torsion-free Λ′_𝒪-module; in particular it is a semilocal ring complete for its radical, the product of its localisations at its finitely many maximal ideals.
hypotheses: [F : ℚ] even.
Use L5/hida-freeness only after supplying its corrected finite-generation/projectivity input on every torsion-character factor; it is currently a gap.
proofSteps: Choose a prime ℓ ∤ 6 unramified in F such that V = U ∩ U(ℓ) acts freely modulo F^× (Skinner–Wiles Lemma 3.5, requested from R18.3).
Pullback H⁰(X(U_a)) → H⁰(X(V_a)) is injective and commutes with the traces in a, so M_∞(U) ↪ M_∞(V), compatibly with T_∞(V, 𝒪) → T_∞(U, 𝒪); hence it is a map of Λ′_𝒪-modules.
M_∞(V) is free of finite rank (hida-freeness), so M_∞(U) is finite and torsion-free over the Noetherian Λ′_𝒪.

T_∞(U, 𝒪) acts faithfully on M_∞(U) (each T₂(U_a, 𝒪) acts faithfully on eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)⁺, dual to its level-a quotient), so T_∞(U, 𝒪) ↪ End_{Λ′_𝒪}(M_∞(U)) is finite and torsion-free; finite over the complete local Λ′_𝒪 makes it semilocal and complete.
acceptance: No freeness of T_∞(U, 𝒪) over Λ′_𝒪 is claimed; only M_∞(V) is free.

nodes.title: Hida's control theorem for nearly ordinary Hilbert forms
nodes.statement: (Skinner–Wiles Proposition 3.7, Hida [H2, Corollary 2.5].) Let F have even degree. If λ : T_∞(U, 𝒪) → Q̄_p is an 𝒪-algebra homomorphism with λ|_{Z(U)} = ψε^μ, μ ≥ 0, where ψ and φ = λ|_{(𝒪_F⊗ℤ_p)^×} have finite order, then there is a nearly ordinary cuspidal automorphic representation π of parallel weight k = (μ + 2)·t such that λ(T(ℓ)) and λ(S(ℓ)) are the T(ℓ)- and S(ℓ)-eigenvalues of the newform of π for every prime ℓ ∤ p with U_ℓ = GL₂(𝒪_{F,ℓ}). The kernels of such λ are the algebraic primes of weight k.
hypotheses: [F : ℚ] even; ε is the cyclotomic character, viewed on Z(U) through reciprocity Z(U) → Gal(F^{(p)}/F).
Use L5/hida-freeness only after supplying its corrected finite-generation/projectivity input on every torsion-character factor; it is currently a gap.
proofSteps: For μ = 0 the statement is the weight-two correspondence: λ factors through some T₂(U_a, 𝒪) by the definition of T_∞, and T₂(U_a, 𝒪) acts on the v-good vectors of π ∈ Π^{n.o.}_2(U_a) (Skinner–Wiles p. 37).
For μ > 0 Skinner–Wiles cite Hida [H2, Corollary 2.5] without proof; the proof is recorded as a gap.
acceptance: Weights are parallel here: the torus character φ has finite order. Non-parallel weights need λ|_{torus} algebraic, which Proposition 3.7 does not treat.

nodes.title: Weight-two algebraic primes are dense on every component
nodes.statement: (Skinner–Wiles Lemma 3.8 and Corollary 3.9.) Let Q be a minimal prime of T_∞(U, 𝒪) and 𝒳(Q) the set of algebraic primes of weight 2 containing Q. Then 𝒳(Q) is Zariski dense in Spec(T_∞(U, 𝒪)/Q). Consequently, if V ⊇ U and for all P in a Zariski-dense subset of 𝒳(Q) some λ ∈ ℋ(P) factors through T_∞(U, 𝒪) → T_∞(V, 𝒪), then Q is the inverse image of a minimal prime of T_∞(V, 𝒪).
hypotheses: [F : ℚ] even; ℋ(P) is the finite set of λ with kernel P.
Use L5/hida-freeness only after supplying its corrected finite-generation/projectivity input on every torsion-character factor; it is currently a gap.
proofSteps: T_∞(U, 𝒪)/Q is a domain, finite and torsion-free over Λ′_𝒪 (hida-hecke-finite), so Λ′_𝒪 ↪ T_∞/Q is a finite injective extension and Spec(T_∞/Q) → Spec Λ′_𝒪 is surjective (lying over).
Every prime of T_∞/Q over a weight-two arithmetic point of Λ′_𝒪 is the kernel of some λ with finite-order restrictions, hence algebraic of weight 2 (hida-control-nearly-ordinary with μ = 0).

The weight-two points of Λ′_𝒪 are dense (totally-real-weight-algebra). If the closure of 𝒳(Q) were a proper closed subset of the irreducible Spec(T_∞/Q), its image would be a closed subset of smaller dimension containing a dense set, which is impossible.

Corollary 3.9: the λ factoring through T_∞(V, 𝒪) on a dense set put Q inside the closed set cut out by ker(T_∞(U) → T_∞(V))-compatible primes; a minimal prime of T_∞(V, 𝒪) below a generic point pulls back to Q.
acceptance: Skinner–Wiles call the density 'immediate' after the Λ′_𝒪 statement; the lying-over and dimension step is spelled out here.

nodes.title: The ordinary family modular-symbol module M_m
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, N prime to p, T*_N (resp. T_N) Hida's universal ordinary Hecke algebra of tame level N acting on all (resp. cuspidal) forms, and m a maximal ideal of T*_N whose residual representation ρ̄_m is irreducible. For each r ≥ 0 the relative homology sequence 0 → H₁(X₁(Np^r); ℤ_p) → H₁(X₁(Np^r), C₁(Np^r); ℤ_p) → H̃₀(C₁(Np^r); ℤ_p) → 0 (4.1) remains exact on ordinary parts, and after localising at m the reduced H₀ of the cusps vanishes. So M_m := lim_r H₁(X₁(Np^r); ℤ_p)^ord_m ≅ lim_r H₁(X₁(Np^r), cusps; ℤ_p)^ord_m is a module over (T*_N)_m ≅ (T_N)_m. Complex conjugation on X₁(Np^r) commutes with the Hecke action, and M_m = M⁺_m ⊕ M⁻_m.
hypotheses: p odd (for the ± splitting); ρ̄_m irreducible (so the cusps disappear after localisation and (T*_N)_m = (T_N)_m).
proofSteps: The ordinary projector is exact (L0a), so (4.1) stays exact on ordinary parts; Eisenstein maximal ideals carry the cuspidal H̃₀, and at non-Eisenstein m it vanishes.
The transition maps in r are the corestrictions/traces on homology, compatible with the Hecke action; M_m is their inverse limit.
Complex conjugation commutes with T(ℓ), U_p and the diamond operators on homology; 2 is invertible.
acceptance: M_m is integral (over ℤ_p) and defined before inverting p.
At an Eisenstein m the absolute and relative limits differ; the construction is only claimed for irreducible ρ̄_m.

nodes.title: Control of the family symbol module
nodes.statement: (Hida [17, Theorem 3.1], [19, Theorem 1.9], as used by Emerton–Pollack–Weston.) (lim→_r H₁(Np^r; ℚ_p/ℤ_p)^ord)^Γ ≅ H₁(Np; ℚ_p/ℤ_p)^ord (4.2); and for r, k with ω_{r,k} ⊂ Λ the product of the classical weight-k primes whose character is trivial on 1 + p^rℤ_p, T_N/ω_{r,k}T_N ≅ T_{r,k} (the ordinary Hecke algebra of S_k(Np^r)) and M_m/ω_{r,k}M_m ≅ (M_{r,k})_{m_{r,k}} with M_{r,k} = H₁(Np^r, cusps; L_{k−2}(ℤ_p)).
hypotheses: ρ̄_m irreducible; k ≥ 2.
proofSteps: The Hecke-algebra statement is Hida's control theorem (L0/hida-control-theorem).
The homology statements are Hida's (Invent. Math. 85 (1986), Theorem 3.1; Amer. J. Math. 110 (1988), Theorem 1.9), cited by Emerton–Pollack–Weston without proof; they are recorded as a gap.
acceptance: The comparison with ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L0 is through H₁(Np^r, cusps; L_{k−2}) ≅ the modular symbols Symb(V_{k−2}) (up to the duality of L0).

nodes.title: Freeness of M^±_m: the family period line
nodes.statement: (Emerton–Pollack–Weston Proposition 4.1.1.) If ρ̄_m is irreducible and p-distinguished, each of M⁺_m and M⁻_m is a free (T_N)_m-module of rank one.
hypotheses: ρ̄_m irreducible and p-distinguished (the two characters of ρ̄_m|_{G_{ℚ_p}} are distinct).
proofSteps: Wiles [34, Theorem 2.1] with Theorem 2.1.2: J₁(Np)(ℚ̄)[m]^ord is free of rank 2 over T_N/m (requested from ModularCurvesPartII R14.6).
By (4.2), Hom(M_m, ℚ_p/ℤ_p)[m] ≅ H₁(Np; ℚ_p/ℤ_p)^ord_m[m] ≅ H₁(Np; F_p)^ord_m[m] ≅ J₁(Np)[p][m]^ord, so M_m/mM_m is free of rank 2 over T_N/m.

The ordinary tower is a compact module with a basis of open Hecke submodules. Its finite-dimensional residual quotient and compact Nakayama give finite generation and a surjection T_m²→M_m. Rational ordinary Eichler–Shimura/control identifies M_m[1/p] as free of rank two over T_m[1/p]; the localized surjection is an isomorphism (a square surjection of free modules). Its kernel is therefore p-power torsion, and T_m is ℤ_p-torsion-free, so that kernel is zero. Since p is odd the signs split as finite projectives over the local T_m; rational Eichler–Shimura gives rank one separately for each sign, hence both are free of rank one. Rank two of their direct sum alone would not prove the two sign ranks.
acceptance: Without p-distinguishedness M^±_m need not be free; the family period is then a module, not a line.

nodes.title: Family periods as trivialisations of an invertible module
nodes.statement: Under family-symbol-free-rank-one, a family period for sign ± is a coordinate isomorphism θ^±:M^±_m→T_m. Two such maps differ by T_m^×. At a classical prime ℘ its inverse at 1 generates the rank-one homology eigenquotient M^±_m⊗_{T_m}O(℘), fixing EPW’s quotient convention for canonical periods up to O(℘)^×. Identifying this normalization with the saturated cohomological eigensymbol lattice of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L1 requires an integral Hecke-compatible duality/control comparison; it does not follow from tensor specialization or rational Eichler–Shimura alone.
hypotheses: ρ̄_m irreducible and p-distinguished.
proofSteps: Freeness gives a coordinate isomorphism θ^±:M^±_m→T_m, whose inverse sends 1 to a basis; two coordinate maps differ by multiplication by a unit.

Specialize the free rank-one homology module and use ordinary control to get its eigenquotient generator. To compare with the saturated eigensymbol line, supply the integral perfect pairing with the correct dual/divided-power coefficient lattice and identify the annihilator eigenline with the dual of this quotient. Track torsion and possible congruence or factorial denominators. This comparison is a recorded gap; no equality of the two integral lattices is asserted before it is supplied.
acceptance: A period line is not a globally chosen basis: θ^± is data, and statements depending on it are equalities up to T_m^× (integrally) or up to O(℘)^× at ℘, not up to a field scalar.
Where M^±_m is not free (p-distinguishedness fails) only the module, not a trivialisation, is available.

nodes.title: The two-variable measure of a Hida family
nodes.statement: The paths [∞, a] on X₁(Np^r), a ∈ P¹(ℚ), give classes in H₁(X₁(Np^r), cusps; ℤ_p) compatible in r; projecting to ordinary parts, localising at m and passing to the limit gives a ↦ {∞, a} ∈ M_m. For a + p^rℤ_p ⊆ ℤ_p^×, µ(a + p^rℤ_p) := U_p^{−r}{∞, a/p^r} ∈ M_m (Definition 4.1.2) is additive (Proposition 4.1.3), hence defines L(m, N) ∈ M_m ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]], with ± components L^±(m, N) ∈ M^±_m ⊗̂ ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]]; after a family period it lies in (T_N)_m[[ℤ_p^×]]. Projecting to the ω^i-part gives L(m, N, ω^i) ∈ (T_N)_m ⊗̂ Λ^{(i)} with sign (−1)^i (the other sign projects to 0).
hypotheses: ρ̄_m irreducible; U_p is invertible on M_m (ordinary part).
proofSteps: Additivity: U_p = Σ_{b mod p}(1 b; 0 p) acts on {∞, a/p^r} as Σ_b {∞, (a + bp^r)/p^{r+1}}, so µ(a + p^rℤ_p) = Σ_b µ(a + bp^r + p^{r+1}ℤ_p).
ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]] is the ring of ℤ_p-valued measures (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1); the completed tensor product uses the m-adic topology on M_m.
The sign of the ω^i-projection: the involution z ↦ −z on ℤ_p^× corresponds to complex conjugation.
acceptance: U_p^{−r} makes sense because U_p is a unit on the ordinary part; this is where ordinarity is used.
L(m, N) is integral: no denominators are introduced before a period is chosen.

nodes.title: Specialisation to one-variable p-adic L-functions
nodes.statement: (Emerton–Pollack–Weston Proposition 4.1.4.) Under the hypotheses of family-symbol-free-rank-one, for every classical height-one prime ℘ of (T_N)_m, L^±(m, N)(℘) ∈ O(℘)[[ℤ_p^×]] is the analytic p-adic L-function of the normalised eigenform f_℘ ∈ S_k(Np^∞, O(℘))^ord[κ_℘], computed with respect to a canonical period; f_℘ need not be new, so the specialisation may be imprimitive (Euler factors at primes dividing the tame level of an oldform removed).
hypotheses: ρ̄_m irreducible and p-distinguished; ℘ classical of weight k ≥ 2.
proofSteps: The one-variable construction µ_{r,k}(a + p^nℤ_p) = U_p^{−n}{∞, a/p^n} ∈ (M_{r,k})_{m_{r,k}} gives L^±_p(m_{r,k}, N).
(M_{r,k})^±_{m_{r,k}} is free of rank one over (T_{r,k})_{m_{r,k}} by control and family-symbol-free-rank-one; the family period induces its trivialisation.

The compatible measures specialize to the one-variable homology-quotient construction of EPW Proposition4.1.4. Thus the resulting scalar function uses the specialized canonical quotient period. Comparison with ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L2’s saturated-eigensymbol normalization needs the integral duality/control input of family-period-line; do not identify the normalizations solely by their interpolation formulas.
acceptance: The equality is up to O(℘)^× (the canonical period), not up to a field scalar.

For the primitive/newform function use the branch construction L1/branch-l-functions and its integral degeneracy-map comparison. The saturated eigensymbol-period convention requires the integral comparison gap of L1/family-period-line.

nodes.title: Locally finite endomorphisms of complete modules
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m and finite residue field, and let M be an R-module that is m-adically separated and complete (M ≅ lim_n M/mⁿM; no finiteness of M is assumed). An R-linear endomorphism T of M is locally finite if for every n ≥ 1 and every v ∈ M/mⁿM the R-submodule of M/mⁿM spanned by the orbit {T^k v : k ≥ 0} is finitely generated; equivalently, each M/mⁿM is the directed union of its T-stable finitely generated R-submodules. Since R/mⁿ is finite, a finitely generated R/mⁿ-module is a finite set, so each such submodule is finite.
hypotheses: R complete noetherian local with finite residue field; M m-adically separated and complete; T ∈ End_R(M).
proofSteps: The two formulations agree: the span of an orbit is T-stable, and a sum of finitely many T-stable finitely generated submodules is again one.
A finitely generated R/mⁿ-module is finite as a set because R/mⁿ has finite length and finite residue field (Ideal.finite_quotient_pow).
acceptance: A finite R-module carries only locally finite endomorphisms; the notion is new only for modules that are not finitely generated, such as completed direct sums of copies of R or completed cohomology.

sources.match: Defines local finiteness on m_R-adically separated complete modules by finite generation of orbit spans modulo every power of m_R, and restates it as M/mⁿ being an inductive limit of finite T-stable modules.
The same definition, phrased as: each M/mⁿ is an inductive limit of finite type T-stable submodules.

nodes.title: Stability of local finiteness under extensions, quotients and products
nodes.statement: Let 0 → M₁ → M₂ → M₃ → 0 be an exact sequence of m-adically separated complete R-modules with compatible endomorphisms T. (1) If T is locally finite on M₁ and M₃, it is locally finite on M₂. (2) If T is locally finite on M₂, it is locally finite on M₃. (3) If T is locally finite on M₂ and mⁿM₂ = 0 for some n, it is locally finite on M₁. Without the bounded-torsion hypothesis (3) fails: on M₂ = ∏_{i≥0} ℤ_p with T(a_0, a_1, …) = (0, p a_0, p² a_1, …, p^i a_{i−1}, …), T is locally finite on M₂ and preserves the kernel M₁ of M₂ → ∏_i ℤ/p^{i(i+1)/2}, but is not locally finite on M₁. (4) If T₁, T₂ commute and are locally finite on M, then T₁T₂ is locally finite.
hypotheses: R complete noetherian local with finite residue field; all modules m-adically separated and complete; T-equivariant maps.
proofSteps: (1): modulo mⁿ, write the image M of M₁/mⁿ in M₂/mⁿ; T is locally finite on M by (2). Given v, local finiteness on M₃ gives T^N v = w + Σ_{i<N} a_i T^i v with w ∈ M, and local finiteness on M gives a relation for w; the span of {T^i v, T^j w} is T-stable and finitely generated.
(2) and (3) are immediate from the definition, since an orbit span in a submodule killed by mⁿ is an orbit span in M₂/mⁿ.

Put r_i=i(i+1)/2 and M₁=∏_i p^{r_i}ℤ_p. The identity r_i=r_{i−1}+i shows that T preserves M₁ and, under (b_i) ↦ (p^{r_i}b_i), acts as the right shift. Modulo p the orbit of the first coordinate vector is linearly independent. On M₂, T is zero modulo p, so locally-finite-mod-maximal proves local finiteness there. T need not map all of M₂ into M₁.
(4): reduce to M killed by mⁿ; the span of {T₂^i T₁^j v} is finitely generated and T₁T₂-stable.
acceptance: The counterexample uses r_i=i(i+1)/2, including the trivial i=0 quotient. It asserts stability of M₁, not T(M₂)⊆M₁. Completeness uses each module’s intrinsic p-adic filtration.

sources.match: Parts (1)–(3) with the proof of (1), and the product-of-ℤ_p counterexample showing that (3) needs the bounded-torsion hypothesis.
Products of commuting locally finite operators are locally finite, by reduction to mⁿ-torsion modules.

nodes.title: Local finiteness is detected modulo the maximal ideal
nodes.statement: For an m-adically separated complete R-module M and T ∈ End_R(M), T is locally finite on M if and only if the induced endomorphism of M/mM is locally finite.
hypotheses: R complete noetherian local with finite residue field; M m-adically separated and complete.
proofSteps: Necessity is part (2) of L0a/locally-finite-stability.

Sufficiency by induction on n, using the right exact sequence (m^{n−1}/mⁿ) ⊗_R M → M/mⁿM → M/m^{n−1}M → 0: the left term is a quotient of a finite direct sum of copies of M/mM (m^{n−1}/mⁿ is a finite-dimensional R/m-space), so T is locally finite on it and on its image, and part (1) of L0a/locally-finite-stability applies to the image and the quotient.
acceptance: For M = ℤ_p^{(ℕ)} completed and T the shift, the criterion fails modulo p, matching not_isLocallyFiniteEnd_shift.

nodes.title: The ordinary projector of a locally finite endomorphism
nodes.statement: Let T be a locally finite endomorphism of an m-adically separated complete R-module M. For every v ∈ M the sequence T^{N!}v converges m-adically; e(T)v := lim_N T^{N!}v defines an R-linear idempotent e = e(T) ∈ End_R(M) commuting with T, and M = eM ⊕ (1 − e)M with both summands T-stable and closed, T bijective on eM and topologically nilpotent on (1 − e)M (for each v ∈ (1 − e)M and each n, Tᵏv ∈ mⁿM for k large). e is the unique idempotent with these properties. When every M/mⁿM is finite, e coincides with the projector of L0a/profinite-ordinary-projector for the quotient system (mⁿM)_n.
hypotheses: T ∈ End_R(M) locally finite (L0a/locally-finite-action).
proofSteps: Fix n and v ∈ M/mⁿM; the orbit span V of v is a finite T-stable module, so L0a/finite-ordinary-projector gives T^{N!}v = e_V v for N ≥ |V|, independent of the choice of V by L0a/ordinary-projector-natural applied to inclusions of finite T-stable submodules.
The resulting projectors on the M/mⁿM are compatible in n (naturality for the reduction maps), and m-adic completeness assembles them into e on M.

Bijectivity of T on eM, topological nilpotence on (1 − e)M and uniqueness are checked modulo each mⁿ on finite T-stable submodules, where they are L0a/ordinary-part-bijective and L0a/finite-ordinary-decomposition-unique.
acceptance: No uniform exponent N with e = T^{N!} on all of M is asserted; on the diagonal example of L0a/locally-finite-action, e is the projection onto the e_0-coordinate and T^{N!} differs from it at every finite N.

sources.match: Existence and uniqueness of e = lim T^{N!} with the decomposition, proved by reduction to a finite R/mⁿ-module where the factorial powers are eventually constant.
The same statement, quoted from Pilloni, with e(T) called the ordinary projector attached to T.

nodes.title: Functoriality and exactness of locally finite ordinary parts
nodes.statement: Let f : M₁ → M₂ be a T-equivariant R-linear map of m-adically separated complete modules on which T is locally finite. (1) f e = e f, so f(eM₁) ⊆ eM₂ and f((1 − e)M₁) ⊆ (1 − e)M₂. (2) If M₃ = coker f is m-adically separated and complete, coker(eM₁ → eM₂) = eM₃. (3) If T is locally finite on M₀ = ker f, then ker(eM₁ → eM₂) = eM₀.
hypotheses: T locally finite on M₁ and M₂ (and on M₀ for (3)); the cokernel separated and complete for (2).
proofSteps: Since f commutes with T, it commutes with each T^{N!}, hence with their limit e (continuity of f for the m-adic topologies).
Thus f is the direct sum of ef and (1 − e)f, which gives (2) and (3); T is locally finite on M₃ by L0a/locally-finite-stability (2).
acceptance: For the inclusion pℤ_p → ℤ_p with T = multiplication by a unit, both ordinary parts are everything and the cokernel ℤ/p is its own ordinary part.

sources.match: Naturality of the projector and its compatibility with cokernels and kernels, from the decomposition of f.

nodes.title: Locally finite endomorphisms of complete flat complexes
nodes.statement: Let C^flat(R) be the category of bounded complexes of flat m-adically separated complete R-modules and D^flat(R) the full subcategory of D(R) of objects they represent (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7, complete flat complexes). A chain endomorphism T of M• ∈ C^flat(R) is locally finite if it is locally finite on every term Mⁱ; then the degreewise projectors form a chain idempotent e(T). An endomorphism T of an object M• of D^flat(R) is locally finite if it has a representative (M•₀, T₀) with M•₀ ∈ C^flat(R) and T₀ a locally finite chain endomorphism. Characterisation (Pilloni Proposition 2.3.1): T is locally finite if and only if the pair (M•, T) admits a complete flat complex with a chain endomorphism representing T, and T acts locally finitely on every Hⁱ(M• ⊗^L_R R/m).
hypotheses: R complete noetherian local with finite residue field.
proofSteps: Degreewise projectors commute with the differentials because the differentials are T-equivariant (L0a/locally-finite-projector-exactness (1)).
Characterisation, forward direction: Hⁱ(M•₀ ⊗ R/m) is a subquotient of Mⁱ₀/m, so L0a/locally-finite-stability applies.

Converse: replace a representative M•₀ by a minimal complete flat subcomplex N• that is a deformation retract (differentials zero modulo m), using the splitting of a complete flat map into an isomorphism and a part vanishing modulo m; the transferred endomorphism s T₀ i acts on Nⁱ/m = Hⁱ(M• ⊗ R/m) as T does, hence is locally finite by L0a/locally-finite-mod-maximal.
acceptance: On a perfect complex every endomorphism is locally finite (Remark 2.3.1), so the notion adds nothing in D^perf(R) and is needed only for complexes of non-finitely-generated complete flat modules.

sources.locator: §2.2, p. 8, and §2.3, Definitions 2.3.1–2.3.2 and Proposition 2.3.1 with Lemma 2.3.1, pp. 9–10

nodes.title: The ordinary direct factor of a locally finite derived endomorphism
nodes.statement: Let T be a locally finite endomorphism of M• ∈ D^flat(R). A locally finite representative (M•₀, T₀) gives the chain idempotent e₀ = e(T₀) and the direct factor ē₀M• of M• in D(R) represented by e₀M•₀. If ē₀M• lies in D^perf(R), then for any other locally finite representative (M•₁, T₁), ē₁M• also lies in D^perf(R) and the canonical map ē₀M• → ē₁M• is a quasi-isomorphism; the ordinary direct factor e(T)M• ∈ D^perf(R) is therefore well defined up to canonical isomorphism, although the idempotent itself is only defined on representatives. When M• is perfect it agrees with the Khare–Thorne ordinary part of L0a/derived-ordinary-idempotent.
hypotheses: T locally finite on M• ∈ D^flat(R); ē₀M• perfect for one representative.
proofSteps: On each Hⁱ(M• ⊗^L R/m) the operators T₀ and T₁ induce the same locally finite endomorphism; by L0a/locally-finite-projector-exactness the projectors induced by e₀ and e₁ both equal its ordinary projector there, so ē₀M• → ē₁M• is an isomorphism modulo m.
ē₁M• is perfect because its reduction modulo m has finite cohomology (complete flat complexes with finite residual cohomology are perfect).
A map of complete flat complexes that is a quasi-isomorphism modulo m is a quasi-isomorphism.
On a perfect M• the endomorphism algebra is finite over R and the factorial-power idempotent is unique (Pilloni Remark 2.3.1), which identifies the construction with L0a/derived-ordinary-idempotent.
acceptance: The statement asserts independence of the direct factor up to canonical quasi-isomorphism, never equality of idempotents in End_{D(R)}(M•) for non-perfect M•.

nodes.title: Ordinary projectors over complete semilocal coefficient rings
nodes.statement: Let R be a Jacobson-adically separated complete semilocal noetherian ring whose quotient by its Jacobson radical is finite (for example Λ = ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]] for odd p, a product of p − 1 complete local rings ℤ_p[[1 + pℤ_p]]). Then R = ∏_j R_j with each R_j complete local with finite residue field, every Jacobson-adically separated complete R-module M decomposes as ∏_j M_j, and an endomorphism T is locally finite when each component T_j is; the ordinary projector, the derived ordinary direct factor and their properties are defined factor by factor, with 'perfect' read as 'bounded complex of finite projective R-modules' (finite projective modules over R need not be free when the factors have different ranks).
hypotheses: R is noetherian semilocal, separated and complete for J=rad(R), with R/J finite; M is J-adically separated and complete. For complexes impose these hypotheses degreewise, together with flatness and boundedness.
proofSteps: For the finitely many maximal ideals m_j, their powers are pairwise comaximal and Jⁿ=∏_j m_jⁿ=⋂_j m_jⁿ. Chinese remaindering followed by J-adic completeness gives R≅∏_j lim_n R/m_jⁿ. Each factor is complete local; its central idempotent decomposes modules and their filtrations. IHG.2 supplies the finite-algebra special case, and this argument supplies the stated generality.
All constructions of L0a/locally-finite-ordinary-projector and L0a/derived-ordinary-direct-factor commute with finite products.
acceptance: For R = ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]] the decomposition has exactly p − 1 factors, indexed by the characters of μ_{p−1}.

nodes.title: Characteristic polynomials of endomorphisms of finite projective modules
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, V a finite projective A-module of constant rank d and f ∈ End_A(V). The characteristic polynomial Q_f(X) := D(1 − X f) ∈ A[X] is the value of the degree-d determinant law of the finite projective A[X]-module A[X] ⊗_A V at 1 − X·(1 ⊗ f); it has constant term 1 and degree at most d, its leading coefficient is (−1)^d det f, it commutes with base change A → A′, it agrees with det(1 − X M) for the matrix M of f in any basis when V is free, and it satisfies Cayley–Hamilton in the reciprocal form X^d Q_f(1/X)|_{X = f} = 0 in End_A(V).
hypotheses: V finite projective of constant rank d (Module.rankAtStalk constant).
proofSteps: The determinant law of a finite projective constant-rank module is IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0 (top exterior power is invertible, endomorphisms of it are scalars, glued from local trivialisations).
Base change of the law and its agreement with Matrix.det on a basis give the formula det(1 − X M) on free modules and the comparison with Mathlib's LinearMap.charpoly (charpoly f = X^d Q_f(1/X)).

Cayley–Hamilton holds Zariski-locally on Spec A, where V is free (LinearMap.aeval_self_charpoly), hence globally since End_A(V) embeds in the product of its localisations; alternatively it is the Cayley–Hamilton identity for the determinant law.
acceptance: This closes the earlier gap 'Characteristic polynomials over finite projective modules'; slope-polynomials uses Q_f.
Import the finite-projective determinant law from its existing owner; this is the spectral-polynomial instance and normalization comparison, not a second generic construction.

sources.match: Buzzard uses the reversed characteristic polynomial on the finite-projective slope summand. This node specializes the determinant-law and Cayley–Hamilton targets already owned by IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants; it plans their comparison with Mathlib’s free-module characteristic polynomial, not another determinant construction.

nodes.title: The spectral hypersurface of a compact endomorphism of a complex
nodes.statement: Let A be a reduced affinoid algebra over a complete non-archimedean field K ⊇ ℚ_p, M• a bounded complex of projective Banach A-modules (direct summands of orthonormalisable ones) and U ∈ End_{K^proj(A)}(M•) compact, i.e. represented by a chain endomorphism Ũ that is compact in every degree. The characteristic series P̃(X) = ∏_k det(1 − X Ũ | M^k) is an entire series over A (the product, not the alternating product, so that every eigenvalue in every degree is seen). Its zero locus Z̃ ⊆ Sp(A) × A¹ carries a complex of coherent sheaves 𝓜• (the universal generalised eigenspace complex of Ũ): Z̃ has an admissible cover by affinoids Y finite and flat over their image V ⊆ Sp(A), with Y a union of connected components of Z̃ ×_{Sp A} V, and on such Y the complex 𝓜•|_Y is the finite slope subcomplex of M•|_V cut out by the factor of P̃ attached to Y, a perfect complex of O(V)-modules.
hypotheses: A reduced affinoid; M• bounded with projective Banach terms; Ũ compact in each degree.
proofSteps: In each degree apply the Fredholm theory of compact operators on projective Banach modules (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4); the characteristic series of the complex is the product of the degreewise ones.

The admissible cover by finite flat spectral blocks is L2a/admissible-slope-cover applied to P̃; on a block the Riesz factorisation P̃ = Q·S gives Ũ-stable decompositions Mᵏ = N_Q(Mᵏ) ⊕ F_Q(Mᵏ) compatible with the differentials, and the finite slope subcomplex N_Q(M•) is a bounded complex of finite projective O(V)-modules (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4, the finite-slope subcomplex and its perfect model).
𝓜•|_Y is N_Q(M•) viewed over O(Y) = O(V)[X]/(Q) with X acting as Ũ⁻¹; the identifications glue by the compatibility of Riesz projectors under refinement.
acceptance: For a complex concentrated in one degree the construction is L2a/spectral-hypersurface.

nodes.title: The spectral variety of a compact endomorphism in the homotopy category
nodes.statement: With M•, U and a compact representative Ũ as in L2a/complex-spectral-hypersurface, the cohomology sheaves 𝓗ⁱ(𝓜•) are coherent on Z̃. Let 𝓘 ⊆ O_{Z̃} be the annihilator of the graded module ⊕_i 𝓗ⁱ(𝓜•). The spectral variety of (M•, U) is the closed subspace Z = V(𝓘) ⊆ Z̃, with the graded coherent sheaf 𝓗•(𝓜•) supported on it. Z and 𝓗•(𝓜•) on Z depend only on U ∈ End_{K^proj(A)}(M•), not on the representative Ũ; the cohomology sheaves have slope decompositions, and at a rank-one point x of Sp(A) the fibre cohomology Hⁱ(M•_x) has slope decompositions for U.
hypotheses: As in L2a/complex-spectral-hypersurface.
proofSteps: Coherence: on a block, 𝓗ⁱ(𝓜•) is the cohomology of a bounded complex of finite O(Y)-modules.

Independence of Ũ: two compact representatives are homotopic through a compact homotopy; on any finite slope window the finite slope subcomplexes are homotopy equivalent (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4, homotopy invariance on a slope window), so their cohomology sheaves are isomorphic over the common blocks and the annihilators agree.
The extra components of Z̃ coming from a contractible summand (as in the cone test) carry zero cohomology and are removed in Z.
acceptance: Local constancy of x ↦ Σ_i (−1)ⁱ dim Hⁱ(M•_x)_{=h} on rank-one points is LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4/finite-slope-euler-local-constancy, cited, not replanned; the neighbourhoods need not cover Sp(A) (Pilloni's footnote 20).

sources.match: Defines Z as the vanishing locus of the annihilator of the cohomology of the universal eigenspace complex, states its independence of Ũ, and proves local constancy of the slope-h Euler characteristic at rank-one points from that of the degreewise slope-h dimensions.

nodes.title: The coherent eigenmodule sheaf on an eigenvariety
nodes.statement: In the setting of L2a/global-weight-gluing (reduced rigid weight space W, linked (Pr) Banach modules, compact controlling operator φ, commuting Hecke algebra 𝐓), the finite projective slope summands N(Y) of the spectral blocks Y, viewed as T(Y)-modules, glue to a coherent sheaf 𝓜 on the eigenvariety D with 𝓜(D(Y)) = N(Y). On every weight chart it is finite projective as an O(V)-module, hence torsion-free in the nonzerodivisor sense over the reduced weight base, its formation commutes with flat base change of the weight space, and for a point w of W and a point x of D over w with residue field L, the localisation at x of the weight-specialised module N(Y)⊗_{O(V)}L is the generalised eigenspace (M_w ⊗ L)^{≤h}[x] of the specialised Banach module. The map 𝐓 ⊗ k(w) → End(𝓜 ⊗ k(w)) has image the Hecke algebra of the fibre, and the surjection from the fibre of O_D at w onto it has nilpotent kernel; D is not asserted reduced, and the nilpotents of the fibre algebra are retained.
hypotheses: The data of L2a/global-weight-gluing; slopes bounded on each chart.
proofSteps: On a chart D(Y) = Sp T(Y), the module N(Y) is finite projective over A and a faithful T(Y)-module, hence a coherent sheaf on D(Y).
Under refinement of blocks and restriction of affinoids, the Riesz projectors are compatible (L2a/hecke-chart-gluing), giving gluing data for the N(Y).

Fibres: Riesz decompositions commute with specialisation (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4 completed base change), so N(Y) ⊗ k(w) is the slope part of the fibre; localising at x gives the generalised eigenspace.

The map T(Y)⊗_A L onto its image in End_L(N(Y)⊗_A L) is surjective by definition, and its kernel is nilpotent by the Cayley–Hamilton argument of Buzzard Lemma 5.10 (localise at the prime kernel of A→L, reduce, then extend the residue field). Equality of semisimplifications by itself would not prove this kernel statement.
acceptance: This answers the earlier gap 'Coherent eigenmodules and nonflat specialization' for the eigenmodule itself; Tor terms for cohomology in several degrees are the complex version, L2a/complex-spectral-variety.

sources.match: The finite projective pieces over the Hecke charts and the description of points; the coherent sheaf is assembled from the same pieces.

Supplies the torsion-freeness and characteristic-polynomial nilimmersion arguments. This author copy has no Lemme 6.6; the specialisation-kernel result is directly Buzzard Lemma 5.10 and Bellaïche Lemma 3.17.
Uses Chenevier's lemma in the modular-symbol case: the specialisation map of Hecke algebras is surjective with nilpotent kernel.

nodes.title: Families of locally analytic distributions over an affinoid of weight space
nodes.statement: Let W = Sp R be an affinoid subdomain of the weight space 𝒲 of continuous characters of ℤ_p^×, with universal character κ_W : ℤ_p^× → R^×. For r ∈ p^ℤ, r ≤ 1, let A[r] be the affinoid algebra of the closed neighbourhood {z ∈ ℂ_p : |z − a| ≤ r for some a ∈ ℤ_p} of ℤ_p, with sup norm, and D[r] its continuous dual. The completed tensor products R ⊗̂ A[r] and R ⊗̂ D[r] are orthonormalisable Banach R-modules with a natural continuous evaluation map R ⊗̂ D[r] → Hom_R,cont(R ⊗̂ A[r], R), which is not asserted to be surjective; for r₁ > r₂ the restriction R ⊗̂ A[r₁] → R ⊗̂ A[r₂] and the dual map R ⊗̂ D[r₂] → R ⊗̂ D[r₁] are compact. The monoid Σ₀(p) of integral matrices (a b; c d) with p ∤ a, p | c and ad − bc ≠ 0 acts on R ⊗̂ A[r] by (γ·f)(z) = κ_W(a + cz) f((b + dz)/(a + cz)) and on the full continuous dual by transposition. The tensor module R ⊗̂ D[r] has the action constructed by bounded multiplication of κ_W(a+cz) on the weight-zero transformed distribution; for every w ∈ W(ℚ_p) the specialisation along w : R → ℚ_p identifies these with A_w[r] and D_w[r] carrying the weight-w action.
hypotheses: p is odd. W=Sp(R) is an analytic weight chart and r∈p^ℤ, 0<r≤1, is chosen so κ_W(a+cz) belongs to R ⊗̂ A[r] for every γ∈Σ₀(p). On the central logarithmic chart with exponent coordinate of norm≤1, κ_W(x)=ω(x)^i exp(T log⟨x⟩) has this property. A general affinoid and high-conductor finite-order weights require smaller analytic radii and suitable local charts; being in one connected component alone does not prove it.
proofSteps: Orthonormalisability: norms of elements of A[r] lie in |ℚ_p^×| when r ∈ p^ℤ, so A[r] and D[r] are orthonormalisable (Serre), and completed tensor products with R stay so.
Compactness of the restriction maps between radii is the classical compactness of restriction of affinoid functions to a strictly smaller disc.

Choose a deep enough subgroup 1+p^{m+1}ℤ_p so the universal character’s value on γ^{p^m} lies uniformly within the p-adic exponential radius. Log/exp on this subgroup and finitely many cosets give an analytic radius r(W)>0; retain r≤min(1,r(W)). This avoids the invalid global exponentiation claim of the later Lemma3.3. The bounded bilinear multiplication A[r]×D[r]→D[r] extends to A[r](R)×D[r](R)→D[r](R). Define (b⊗μ)|γ=κ_W(a+cz)·(b⊗(μ|₀γ)) on the dense tensor subspace and extend continuously. Associativity gives the monoid action, and coefficient specialization gives the weight-w action. No identification with the full R-valued dual is used.
acceptance: At integral weights the specialised action is the weight-k action of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L2, so the classical distribution modules are recovered.

nodes.title: Families of distribution-valued modular symbols with compact U_p
nodes.statement: For N prime to p and Γ=Γ₁(N)∩Γ₀(p), the family symbols Hom_Γ(Δ₀,D[r](R)) have the closed finite Manin-generators presentation. On a nice chart in the sense of the later author Definition3.4 (R and its unit-ball reduction principal ideal domains), the closed-submodule argument of Lemma3.7 proves potential orthonormalisability. The Hecke operators are continuous and U_p factors through radius improvement; the bounded restriction argument of Proposition3.6 supplies compactness and links. For the dagger family D†[r](R), compactly supported cohomology gives an injective specialization map. It is an isomorphism except at weight0 with negative sign, where the cokernel is the one-dimensional E₂ Hecke module. Passing to adapted slope≤ν pieces retains this exception exactly when ν≥1. General affinoid coefficient charts require the corresponding Banach hypothesis/descent interface; no unrestricted closed-submodule theorem is asserted.
hypotheses: N prime to p; p odd; an analytic coefficient chart and 0<r≤r(W).

For potential orthonormalisability use the exact nice-chart hypotheses of the later Definition3.4 and Lemma3.7, or a separately supplied equivalent Banach hypothesis. For dagger coefficients use 0≤r<r(W).
The global chart/descent extension is an explicit input; the source proves these statements on nice neighbourhoods of classical integer weights.
proofSteps: Choose finitely many Manin generators; their evaluations embed symbols as a closed submodule of a finite power of D[r](R). On a nice chart, reduction of its unit ball embeds into the ambient free reduction module; the coefficient reduction is a PID, so this submodule is free. Lift a residue basis and complete to obtain an orthonormalisation (later Lemma3.7, p.28). This uses the PID reduction hypothesis, not merely closedness.

Use the bounded U_p radius improvement and the compact restriction of Proposition3.6, pp.27–28, with companions proving the link relations. The global Banach descent needed beyond these nice charts remains a separate input.

For the weight quotient u=0, apply the compact-support long exact sequence to 0→D†(R)→^u D†(R)→D†_w→0. Poincaré duality identifies the obstruction with u-torsion in H₀(Γ,D†(R)); later Lemma3.9 computes it as zero away from weight0 and as the E₂ module at weight0. The orientation reversal makes its sign negative. Thus Theorem3.10 and Corollary3.12 give the stated cokernel, with U_p=p of slope1.
acceptance: This is an unresolved coefficient-model target. Do not invoke property(Pr), compact U_p or an isomorphism on weight fibres until the gap is supplied. E14 establishes failure of the source proof, not these replacement conclusions.

nodes.title: Finite slope pieces of family modular symbols
nodes.statement: For a slope-adapted analytic chart with the required property(Pr) and compact U_p inputs, Riesz theory gives a finite-projective Hecke-stable family-symbol summand of slope≤ν. At weight w its specialization is the global image Symb^±_Γ(D_w)^{≤ν}_g, defined as the image in the actual weight-w symbols. On nice charts it equals the full slope≤ν space except when w=0, the sign is negative and ν≥1, where the quotient is the one-dimensional E₂ module. Compatible U_p links identify the bounded and dagger radius models on these finite-slope summands.
hypotheses: The chart is slope adapted and carries the Banach coefficient/symbol inputs specified above.
Use the actual specialization exact sequence of family-modular-symbols. A full-symbol isomorphism is permitted only after excluding (w=0, sign−, ν≥1) or localizing away from the E₂ eigensystem.
proofSteps: Riesz theory for compact operators on (Pr) modules (Coleman, Serre, Buzzard), from LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4.

Riesz base change gives the internal family fibre. The compact-support comparison of family-modular-symbols identifies its image in actual weight-w symbols. The E₂ cokernel has U_p=p, so survives precisely for ν≥1 in the negative sign at weight0. Use the global image g without silently identifying it with the full fibre.

Radius independence follows from the link-and-companion relations αc=cα=U_p^m on appropriate radii: U_p is invertible on finite-slope pieces, so these links are isomorphisms there. Compact injectivity alone would not imply surjectivity.
acceptance: The rank of the slope-≤ν piece equals the dimension of every fibre, as the specialisation isomorphism requires.

nodes.title: Local pieces of the modular-symbol eigencurve
nodes.statement: For a slope-adapted nice chart W=Sp R with R a one-dimensional principal ideal domain, let 𝕋^±_{W,ν} be the R-subalgebra of End_R(Symb^±_Γ(D(R))^{≤ν}) generated by T_ℓ (ℓ∤Np), U_p and diamond operators. It is finite and torsion-free, hence flat over R; C^±_{W,ν}=Sp 𝕋^±_{W,ν} has a finite flat weight map. Its Hecke functions are bounded and U_p is invertible with valuation≤ν. At w, define 𝕋^±_{w,ν} using the global-image subspace Symb^±_Γ(D_w)^{≤ν}_g, not the entire actual-symbol space; its geometric points are precisely the Hecke eigensystems in that subspace. These constructions extend to other charts only with the recorded Banach/descent inputs.
hypotheses: (W, ν) adapted; W one-dimensional and connected.

Use the nice-chart coefficient and specialization constructions of L2, with global-image symbol fibres. Extension to arbitrary weight charts requires the explicit global chart/descent gaps. At decent classical refined points the E₂ exception is excluded (positive slope for Eisenstein forms).

At weight0 and negative sign use the global-image subspace g of family-slope-pieces, or localize away from the E₂ eigensystem; do not use an isomorphism with all actual symbols at that exceptional point. For general charts the stipulated symbol-specialization/descent input must supply the same convention.
proofSteps: Finiteness: a subalgebra of the endomorphisms of a finite projective module over a noetherian ring.
Torsion-freeness: it acts faithfully on a torsion-free module; flatness over the Dedekind ring R follows.
This is L2a/finite-hecke-images in the modular instance, with the controlling operator φ = U_p.
acceptance: κ^± is finite and flat, and the ℚ̄_p-points over w are the eigensystems of the fibre (with L2/specialisation-nilpotent-kernel).
All symbol-fibre and eigensystem comparisons use the global-image subspace; the exceptional E₂ quotient is retained explicitly.

nodes.title: Specialisation of Hecke algebras has nilpotent kernel
nodes.statement: For w∈W(ℚ_p), specialization gives a surjection s_w:𝕋^±_{W,ν}⊗_{R,w}ℚ_p→𝕋^±_{w,ν} with nilpotent kernel, where the target acts on the global-image slope subspace. Thus the geometric points of the weight fibre are the eigensystems in Symb^±_Γ(D_w)^{≤ν}_g. Localization at a geometric point gives the corresponding surjection of finite local residue-field algebras with nilpotent kernel. The family fibre algebra and the Hecke image of the specialized module need not be isomorphic. Use the full actual-symbol space only after excluding the exceptional E₂ eigensystem.
hypotheses: (W, ν) adapted; w ∈ W(ℚ_p).
The specialization isomorphism with the global-image subspace in L2/family-slope-pieces is supplied; it does not identify the entire actual-symbol space at the exceptional weight.

Use the nice-chart coefficient and specialization constructions of L2, with global-image symbol fibres. Extension to arbitrary weight charts requires the explicit global chart/descent gaps. At decent classical refined points the E₂ exception is excluded (positive slope for Eisenstein forms).

For general charts the stipulated symbol-specialization/descent input must supply the same convention.
proofSteps: Surjectivity: the image is a subalgebra of 𝕋^±_{w,ν} containing the image of the Hecke operators.

On a local free trivialization of the finite projective slope module, an element of the Hecke image whose specialized matrix is zero has all nonleading characteristic coefficients in the weight maximal ideal. Cayley–Hamilton shows that its image in the specialized Hecke algebra is nilpotent (Buzzard Lemma5.10). The resulting nil ideal is nilpotent because the algebra is finite-dimensional. This requires identification with the global-image symbols g, as stated in the hypotheses; having the same semisimplification would be insufficient.
acceptance: At a point where κ^± is étale and the generalised eigenspace is one-dimensional, s_x is an isomorphism ℚ̄_p → ℚ̄_p.
All symbol-fibre and eigensystem comparisons use the global-image subspace; the exceptional E₂ quotient is retained explicitly.

nodes.title: The eigencurves C^± from overconvergent modular symbols
nodes.statement: Assume an admissible analytic coefficient-chart cover of all weight space with the property(Pr), compact U_p, specialization and compatible radius links of family-slope-pieces. The eigenvariety machine glues C^±_{W,ν} to rigid curves C^± with weight maps κ^± and analytic Hecke functions, with U_p a unit. They are equidimensional of dimension one and the weight maps are locally finite and flat. For a complete extension L/ℚ_p, points over w are the finite-slope eigensystems in the global-image symbol space Symb^±_Γ(D_w)_g⊗L. On the source’s nice charts this is the full symbol space except for the negative-sign E₂ quotient at weight0. The existence of the global chart cover/descent is an explicit gap, not a consequence of the abstract eigenvariety machine.
hypotheses: N prime to p; weight space 𝒲 of continuous characters of ℤ_p^× (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0a).

Use the nice-chart coefficient and specialization constructions of L2, with global-image symbol fibres. Extension to arbitrary weight charts requires the explicit global chart/descent gaps. At decent classical refined points the E₂ exception is excluded (positive slope for Eisenstein forms).

At weight0 and negative sign use the global-image subspace g of family-slope-pieces, or localize away from the E₂ eigensystem; do not use an isomorphism with all actual symbols at that exceptional point. For general charts the stipulated symbol-specialization/descent input must supply the same convention.
proofSteps: Construct the local pieces (L2/local-eigencurve-piece) and glue them along restriction and refinement (L2a/hecke-chart-gluing and L2a/global-weight-gluing), the linked Banach modules being the family symbols for nested affinoids.
Points: L2a/eigenpacket-points combined with L2/specialisation-nilpotent-kernel.
Equidimensionality and flatness: each local piece is finite flat over a one-dimensional affinoid, so every component has dimension one.
acceptance: Every refined newform of slope < k + 1 gives a point (L2/small-slope-classicality), and the eigencurve is equidimensional of dimension one.

nodes.title: The coherent eigensymbol sheaf on C^±
nodes.statement: The slope family-symbol modules glue, using the compatible links, to a coherent sheaf 𝓢^± on C^±. It is torsion-free over weight space and its sections over C^±_{W,ν} are the slope family symbols. The local factor at x of its weight-specialized sections is the generalized eigenspace in Symb^±_Γ(D_w)_g. The residue fibre 𝓢^±⊗κ(x) is the quotient of that local factor by its maximal ideal and may have smaller dimension. Evaluation and specialization are compatible sheaf maps. Local freeness is asserted only under the separate rank-one hypotheses; an eigenpacket does not specify an eigenvector. The global-image convention is essential at the exceptional E₂ point.

nodes.title: Classicality of small-slope points of the eigencurve
nodes.statement: Let x be a point of C^± over an integral weight k ≥ 0 with v_p(U_p(x)) < k + 1. Then the specialisation ρ*_k : Symb^±_Γ(D_k) → Symb^±_Γ(V_k) restricts to an isomorphism of generalised eigenspaces at x, Symb^±_Γ(D_k)(x) ≅ Symb^±_Γ(V_k)(x), and x is the eigensystem of a classical p-stabilised form of weight k + 2 and level Γ (cuspidal, or an Eisenstein series of the sign of the ± part). Classical points of slope < k + 1 are Zariski dense in every component of C^±, and accumulate at every classical point of small slope.
hypotheses: x over k ∈ ℤ_{≥0}; slope strictly less than k + 1.

Use the nice-chart coefficient and specialization constructions of L2, with global-image symbol fibres. Extension to arbitrary weight charts requires the explicit global chart/descent gaps. At decent classical refined points the E₂ exception is excluded (positive slope for Eisenstein forms).
proofSteps: Stevens' control theorem (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L2) gives the isomorphism on slope-<k+1 parts; restrict to the x-generalised eigenspace (L2/eigensymbol-sheaf).
Eichler–Shimura (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L0) identifies Symb^±_Γ(V_k) with weight-(k + 2) forms of level Γ, so x is classical.

Density: on a local piece over W, the integral weights k with k + 1 > ν are dense in W, and every component of C^±_{W,ν} is finite flat over W, so its points over those weights are classical and Zariski dense.
acceptance: The slope bound is strict: at slope exactly k + 1 (critical slope) ρ*_k need not be injective on the eigenspace; that case is PadicFamilies L3.

nodes.title: Freeness of family symbols at étale non-critical points
nodes.statement: Let x ∈ C^± lie over an integral weight k with slope < k + 1, corresponding to a refined newform f_β whose generalised eigenspace Symb^±_Γ(V_k)(f_β) is one-dimensional, and assume κ^± is étale at x. Then the localisation of 𝓢^± at x is free of rank one over the local ring O_{C^±,x}, and the weight map induces an isomorphism of the geometric henselian local rings at x and k (or of their completions); consequently, after shrinking, there is a neighbourhood V of x and a family symbol Φ ∈ 𝓢^±(V) whose specialisation at every classical point y ∈ V is a generator of the eigenline of y. This is the local freeness hypothesis required to form scalar-valued families of p-adic L-functions.
hypotheses: x classical of slope < k + 1; newform eigenspace of dimension one; κ^± étale at x.

Use the nice-chart coefficient and specialization constructions of L2, with global-image symbol fibres. Extension to arbitrary weight charts requires the explicit global chart/descent gaps. At decent classical refined points the E₂ exception is excluded (positive slope for Eisenstein forms).
proofSteps: The fibre of 𝓢^± at x is Symb^±_Γ(D_k)(x) ≅ Symb^±_Γ(V_k)(x) (L2/small-slope-classicality), of dimension one.

At the geometric point, étaleness identifies the henselian local branch with the geometric weight DVR. The family module is finite and torsion-free over that DVR, hence free; its one-dimensional weight fibre gives rank one by Nakayama. Ordinary unhenselized local rings need not be literally equal under an étale map.
A generator over a neighbourhood specialises to a nonzero element of each one-dimensional classical eigenline nearby (the eigenspaces are one-dimensional at nearby classical newform points).
acceptance: This is a noncritical sufficient criterion. At a decent critical point, rank-one freeness over the eigencurve still holds by L3/family-symbols-free-rank-one; its weight-fibre dimension is e, not its residue-fibre dimension.

For a cuspidal refined form the generalized eigenspaces in cuspidal forms and symbols have the same dimension. The middle module is the global image: the full negative-sign weight0 symbol module has an extra E₂ quotient that cannot be inserted into this comparison.

proofSteps: Chenevier's comparison theorem for eigenvarieties: two reduced equidimensional eigenvarieties over 𝒲 whose classical structures (Zariski-dense sets of classical points with the same Hecke eigensystems) correspond are related by closed immersions.
The classical structures match by Coleman's control theorem on overconvergent forms and Stevens' control theorem with Eichler–Shimura on symbols (L2/small-slope-classicality).
acceptance: The overconvergent-forms side (Coleman's Banach modules and his control theorem) and Chenevier's comparison theorem are recorded gaps: no roadmap plans Coleman's overconvergent elliptic modular forms; the modular-symbol eigencurve C^± is self-contained without them.
All symbol-fibre and eigensystem comparisons use the global-image subspace; the exceptional E₂ quotient is retained explicitly.

nodes.title: The congruence module of an augmentation
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, O an integral domain and λ : A → O a surjective ring homomorphism with kernel 𝔭_λ. For an ideal J of A and an A-module M write M[J] = {m ∈ M : Jm = 0}, and put I_λ := A[𝔭_λ] = Ann_A(𝔭_λ). The congruence module of M at λ is the O-module Ψ_λ(M) := M / (M[𝔭_λ] + M[I_λ]) (it is killed by 𝔭_λ + I_λ, hence an O/λ(I_λ)-module). It is functorial in A-linear maps, and when (A,λ) is an augmented complete noetherian local O-algebra in Iyengar–Khare–Manning’s C_O(0) (O a complete DVR, A_{𝔭_λ} regular of dimension zero) and M is finitely generated over A, Ψ_λ(M) is a torsion O-module of finite length that agrees, for M of positive depth, with their higher-codimension congruence module Ψ_A(M) in codimension zero.
hypotheses: λ : A → O surjective onto a domain; M any A-module.

For the IKM finite-length comparison: an O-algebra section of λ, A complete noetherian local, A_{𝔭_λ} regular of dimension zero, and M finitely generated. Positive depth is additionally required for the comparison isomorphism.
proofSteps: Functoriality: an A-linear map sends M[J] into M'[J] for every ideal J.

Torsion and finite length when A is regular at 𝔭_λ in codimension zero: after inverting a uniformiser, A ⊗ K splits as K × B with 𝔭_λ and I_λ generating the unit ideal, so M[𝔭_λ] + M[I_λ] has full rank.

Comparison with Iyengar–Khare–Manning: their Proposition 2.10 gives a natural surjection from M/(M[𝔭_λ] + M[I_λ]) onto their Ψ_A(M) with torsion kernel, bijective when depth_A M ≥ 1; their Example 2.11 shows it can fail to be injective in depth zero.
acceptance: This is the generic owner requested by red-team finding RT-AREA-langlands-1/27: AutomorphicCongruences L0, SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.1 and IntegralIwasawaTheory I.5 keep only their Hecke-module instances and cite this node.

nodes.title: The congruence ideal of an augmentation
nodes.statement: For a surjection λ:A→O, put 𝔭_λ=ker λ, I_λ=Ann_A(𝔭_λ), and η_λ=λ(I_λ)⊆O. If Ann_A(I_λ)=𝔭_λ, then Ψ_λ(A)≅O/η_λ. A sufficient case is reduced A finite flat over the domain O with λ an O-algebra surjection: its generic algebra has O’s fraction field as the λ-factor. More generally a reduced Noetherian A with 𝔭_λ a minimal prime has the double-annihilator identity. If O is a complete DVR in the finite-flat case, η_λ is nonzero and O/η_λ has finite length. Finite flatness over some other domain mapping onto O does not by itself give the double-annihilator identity.
hypotheses: λ : A → O surjective; for the identification Ψ_λ(A) ≅ O/η_λ, A reduced with Ann_A(I_λ) = 𝔭_λ.
proofSteps: Ψ_λ(A) = A/(I_λ + Ann_A(I_λ)) = A/(I_λ + 𝔭_λ) ≅ O/λ(I_λ).

For reduced Noetherian A embed A into the product of its minimal-prime fraction fields. If 𝔭_λ is minimal, Ann(𝔭_λ) is the lattice on that generic factor and its annihilator is 𝔭_λ. In the finite-flat O-algebra case λ selects a field factor in A⊗Frac(O), and clearing denominators gives a nonzero element of η_λ. No such factor argument applies merely from flatness over an unrelated base.
acceptance: For the fibre product of two copies of ℤ_p glued modulo pⁿ, η_λ = pⁿℤ_p and Ψ_λ(A) ≅ ℤ/pⁿ.

nodes.title: The reduced Hida algebra T_Σ of a residual representation and its branches
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(k) be irreducible, odd, ordinary, p-distinguished and modular, with a chosen p-stabilisation, N(ρ̄) its tame conductor, and for a finite set Σ of primes ℓ ≠ p let N(Σ) = N(ρ̄)∏_{ℓ∈Σ} ℓ^{m_ℓ} with m_ℓ = dim V^{I_ℓ}. T_Σ = T_Σ(ρ̄) is the localisation of the ordinary Hecke algebra T′_{N(Σ)} (without U_ℓ for ℓ | N(Σ)) at the unique maximal ideal whose residual representation with its p-stabilisation is ρ̄; it is reduced and finite flat over Λ, carries ρ_Σ : G_ℚ → GL₂(T_Σ) with trace ρ_Σ(Frob_ℓ) = T_ℓ for ℓ ∤ N(Σ)p, and Σ ⊆ Σ′ gives a surjection T_{Σ′} → T_Σ. For a minimal prime 𝔞 of T_Σ, T(𝔞) := T_Σ/𝔞 is a local domain finite over Λ; there are a unique divisor N(𝔞) of N(Σ) and a minimal prime 𝔞′ of the new quotient T^new_{N(𝔞)} over 𝔞, and T(𝔞) ↪ T(𝔞)° := T^new_{N(𝔞)}/𝔞′ is an isomorphism after inverting p (and an isomorphism when N(𝔞) = N(ρ̄)).
hypotheses: ρ̄ irreducible, odd, ordinary, p-distinguished and modular; p ≥ 5 is not needed for the definitions.
proofSteps: Existence and uniqueness of the maximal ideal: modularity of ρ̄ and level optimisation; the maximal ideal of T_{N(Σ)} lifting it with T_ℓ ∈ 𝔫 for ℓ ∈ Σ gives an isomorphism of localisations (EPW Proposition 2.6.2).

Reducedness and finite flatness over Λ: T′_{N(Σ)} ⊗_Λ L is a product of new Hecke algebras of levels dividing N(Σ) (EPW Proposition 2.4.2), and the ordinary Hecke algebra is finite flat over Λ (L0/hida-control-theorem).
Branches: minimal primes of T_Σ correspond to local components of T_Σ ⊗_Λ L, each of which comes from a unique new level.
acceptance: T_Σ is reduced and finite flat over Λ, and its minimal primes correspond to Hida families of newforms with a definite tame conductor N(𝔞).

nodes.title: Congruence modules of a branch of a Hida family
nodes.statement: For a branch 𝔞 of T_Σ (L1/reduced-hida-algebra), let λ_𝔞 : T_Σ → T(𝔞) be the quotient map. The family congruence module of an T_Σ-module M is Ψ_{λ_𝔞}(M) (L1/congruence-module, with O replaced by the local domain T(𝔞)) and the family congruence ideal is η_𝔞 = λ_𝔞(Ann_{T_Σ}(𝔞)) ⊆ T(𝔞). Since T_Σ is reduced and finite flat over Λ, Ψ_{λ_𝔞}(T_Σ) ≅ T(𝔞)/η_𝔞, a torsion T(𝔞)-module, and η_𝔞 = T(𝔞) iff Spec T(𝔞) meets no other branch. For the ordinary family symbol module M = M^±_𝔪 ⊗ T_Σ, free of rank one over T_Σ under the hypotheses of L1/family-symbol-free-rank-one, Ψ_{λ_𝔞}(M) ≅ T(𝔞)/η_𝔞 as well, and the choice of a trivialisation of M does not change it. For a primitive cuspidal component, Hida also constructs a Λ-adic congruence module using free closures of the projected Hecke lattices. Its identification with the raw annihilator module above is not asserted without proving those lattices are reflexive. Hida’s free-closure module is a finite torsion module over Λ with principal annihilator (Hida, Theorem 3.6), and for each k ≥ 2 the weight-k module of congruence between the forms belonging to the component and the other ordinary forms of weight k is the kernel of a canonical surjection between the weight-k fibres of Hida's two Λ-adic congruence modules (Hida, Corollary 3.8).
hypotheses: ρ̄ irreducible and p-distinguished (for freeness of M^±_𝔪); 𝔞 a minimal prime of T_Σ.
proofSteps: Reducedness of T_Σ gives Ann(Ann(𝔞)) = 𝔞, hence L1/congruence-ideal's identification.
Freeness of M^±_𝔪 (L1/family-symbol-free-rank-one) transports the computation from T_Σ to M; a different generator changes the isomorphism by a unit, not the module.
η_𝔞 = T(𝔞) iff Ann(𝔞) + 𝔞 = T_Σ iff the branch is a connected component of Spec T_Σ.

Hida’s (3.9) replaces the projected component lattices by their free closures (pp.252–253), whereas Ψ_{λ_𝔞}(T_Σ) uses the raw projected lattices. Compare the inclusion between these quotients and its finite/pseudonull correction; equality requires an additional reflexivity hypothesis. This comparison is a recorded gap.
acceptance: Only the instance is planned here; the generic definition is L1/congruence-module.

nodes.title: Change of trivialisation of the family period line
nodes.statement: Let θ^± : M^±_𝔪 ≅ T_𝔪 be a trivialisation of the invertible family symbol module (L1/family-period-line) and L_θ^± ∈ T_𝔪 ⊗̂ ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]] the scalar two-variable p-adic L-function obtained by applying θ^± to L^±(𝔪, N) (L1/family-measure). If θ′ = u·θ with u ∈ T_𝔪^×, then L_{θ′}^± = u·L_θ^±, and for every classical height-one prime ℘ the specialisations differ by the unit u(℘) ∈ O(℘)^×. Conversely, any two trivialisations differ by such a unit, so the ideal generated by L^±_θ in T_𝔪 ⊗̂ ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]] and the Iwasawa μ- and λ-invariants of its specialisations do not depend on θ; equality with single-form p-adic L-functions built from canonical periods holds up to a unit, never up to an arbitrary scalar in Frac O(℘).
hypotheses: ρ̄_𝔪 irreducible and p-distinguished, so that M^±_𝔪 is free of rank one.
proofSteps: θ′ ∘ θ⁻¹ is a T_𝔪-linear automorphism of T_𝔪, i.e. multiplication by a unit u.
Applying θ is T_𝔪-linear and commutes with the completed tensor product, so the formula follows; specialisation at ℘ is a ring map.

Specialization preserves the homology eigenquotient basis, so EPW’s canonical quotient periods differ by O(℘)^×. Comparison with the saturated integral period lattice of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L1 is conditional on the integral pairing/control input recorded in family-period-line; rational comparison alone permits nonunit denominators.
acceptance: The statement is integral: no p is inverted, and the ambiguity is a unit of T_𝔪, separating equality up to a unit from equality up to a field scalar as the stage requires.

nodes.title: Two-variable p-adic L-functions on the branches of a Hida family
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ be as in L1/reduced-hida-algebra and 0 ≤ i ≤ p − 2, Λ^{(i)} the ω^i-component of ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]]. (1) L_Σ(ρ̄, ωⁱ) ∈ T_Σ ⊗̂ Λ^{(i)} is the image of L(𝔫, N(Σ), ωⁱ) (L1/family-measure) under T_Σ ≅ (T_{N(Σ)})_𝔫, defined up to T_Σ^×; its reductions modulo a height-one prime ℘ and modulo the maximal ideal are defined up to units. (2) For a branch 𝔞, L(ρ̄, 𝔞, ωⁱ) ∈ T(𝔞)° ⊗̂ Λ^{(i)} is the image of L(𝔪, N(𝔞), ωⁱ) under the surjection T_{N(𝔞)} → T^new_{N(𝔞)}/𝔞′ = T(𝔞)°; at a classical height-one prime ℘ of T(𝔞) it specialises to the p-adic L-function of the newform f_℘, whereas L_Σ(ρ̄, ωⁱ)(℘) is that of the Σ-imprimitive oldform g_℘. (3) Comparison: there is an isomorphism T(𝔞)° ⊗ M(N(Σ))_𝔫 ≅ T(𝔞)° ⊗ M(N(𝔞))_𝔪 compatible with complex conjugation carrying L(𝔫, N(Σ)) to L(𝔪, N(𝔞))·E_Σ(𝔞), with E_Σ(𝔞) = ∏_{ℓ∈Σ} E_ℓ(𝔞, ⟨ℓ⟩⁻¹) the product of Euler factors; hence L_Σ(ρ̄, ωⁱ) ≡ u·L(ρ̄, 𝔞, ωⁱ)·E_Σ(𝔞, ωⁱ) modulo 𝔞 for a unit u of T(𝔞)°.
hypotheses: ρ̄ irreducible, odd, ordinary, p-distinguished and modular, with a chosen p-stabilisation; Σ a finite set of primes ℓ ≠ p.

Supply the ordinary residual Wiles–Ihara injectivity and eigenvector-vanishing input of EPW Lemmas4.5.2–4.5.3, pp.39–43, in the precise level/Hecke conventions of Theorem4.3.2; it is not supplied merely by R14.4/degeneracy-cohomology.
proofSteps: (1) and (2) are transports of L1/family-measure along the isomorphism of EPW Proposition 2.6.2 and the surjection (4.4); specialisation is L1/family-measure-specialisation.

Use EPW Theorem4.3.2’s degeneracy-map comparison: its integral isomorphism needs residual injectivity, proved in §4.5 by the Wiles–Ihara degeneracy exact sequence and the full-Hecke-eigenvector vanishing lemma. The mere existence of degeneracy maps is insufficient. Once this isomorphism is supplied, evaluating path classes gives the Euler-factor product and identifies periods up to a unit uniformly, not just pointwise after inverting p.
acceptance: At every classical height-one prime ℘ of T(𝔞), L(ρ̄, 𝔞, ωⁱ) specialises to the p-adic L-function of the newform f_℘ up to a unit (EPW Proposition 4.1.4 with Definition 4.2.2).

nodes.title: Λ-adic forms as q-expansions and their duality with the ordinary Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 5, N = N₀p with p ∤ N₀, Λ = ℤ_p[[X]] with X ↔ γ − 1 for γ = 1 + p, and I a finite flat Λ-algebra. An ordinary Λ-adic cusp form in weight component a of level N with coefficients in I is a formal q-expansion F = Σ_{n≥1} a(n, F)qⁿ ∈ I[[q]] such that for every arithmetic point P of I above P_k = (1 + X − (1 + p)^k) with k ≥ 2 the specialisation F mod P is the q-expansion of a classical ordinary cusp form of weight k and level N₀p with nebentypus ω^{a−k} at points above P_k. They form an I-module S^ord(N,a; I). The pairing (h, F) ↦ a(1, F|h) identifies S^ord(N; Λ) with Hom_Λ(h^ord(N,a; Λ), Λ), and normalised eigenforms in S^ord(N,a; I) correspond to Λ-algebra homomorphisms h^ord(N,a; Λ) → I. This definition does not use the Eisenstein family.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5; N₀ prime to p; specialisation required at every arithmetic point of weight k ≥ 2.
proofSteps: Weight-k duality: Hecke algebras and forms are dual under the first-coefficient pairing at every finite weight and level (L0/hecke-duality).

Freeness and control (L0/hida-control-theorem): h^ord(N; Λ) is free of finite rank and its fibre at P_k is the weight-k ordinary Hecke algebra; hence Hom_Λ(h^ord, Λ) specialises at every P_k to the dual of the weight-k Hecke algebra, i.e. to ordinary cusp forms of weight k, which is the q-expansion condition.

Conversely a family of q-expansions specialising to classical forms defines, through a(1, F|T(n)) = a(n, F), a Λ-linear functional on the Hecke algebra (the Hecke operators act on q-expansions coefficientwise and their action is determined at a Zariski-dense set of weights).
acceptance: Wiles's original definition (Invent. Math. 94, 1988) imposes the classicality condition only at a Zariski-dense set of weights; with Hida's control theorem the two versions agree, and this is the equivalence the stage asks for.

sources.locator: §2, Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 2.2, pp. 245–247; §3, (3.2), Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.2, pp. 249–250
sources.match: The duality between p-adic modular forms and Hecke algebras by the first-coefficient pairing, the continuous Λ-algebra structure of the Hecke algebras, freeness of the ordinary part and the control isomorphisms at every weight; together these give the q-expansion description of the dual of h^ord.

nodes.title: Primitive components of the ordinary Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Let L be the fraction field of Λ_K and h^ord(N; 𝒪_K) the cuspidal ordinary Hecke algebra (p ≥ 5, N = N₀p). The algebra h^ord(N; K) := h^ord(N; 𝒪_K) ⊗_Λ L is a finite-dimensional L-algebra; its primitive part h^ord_prim (the part not coming from lower tame level) is semisimple, a product of finite field extensions 𝒦 of L (the primitive components). If 𝒦 is a primitive cuspidal component with d = [𝒦 : L], then for every k ≥ 2 exactly d ordinary eigenforms of weight k and level Γ₁(N₀p) belong to 𝒦, their associated newforms have conductor divisible by N₀, and conversely every ordinary eigenform of weight k ≥ 2 whose newform has conductor divisible by N₀ belongs to a unique primitive component. The algebraic closure of ℚ_p in 𝒦 is a finite extension of K, and primitive components are compatible with extension of K.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5; N₀ prime to p; cuspidal components.
proofSteps: Semisimplicity: the primitive part of h^ord ⊗ L injects into a product over classical weights of semisimple new Hecke algebras (Hecke operators on newforms are semisimple), so it has no nilradical. Import the full newform eigenproperties and semisimplicity from ModularForms Layer4. The pinned Newform structure alone only carries eigenproperties at good indices.

For a primitive component 𝒦, distinguish the projected Hecke image from its Λ-free closure h(𝒦). Put L=𝒦∩h. Hida’s Theorem3.6 makes L reflexive, hence free over the regular two-dimensional Λ; h/L is torsion-free. At P_k the quotient is free over the DVR Λ_(P_k), so L_(P_k)/P_k is an ideal of the classical ordinary Hecke algebra, annihilating oldforms. Newform semisimplicity makes it a semisimple direct summand. The local projected image and its free closure agree there, so the free closure’s rank-d specialization embeds into this summand and has d geometric eigencharacters. This proves the count, without asserting that an arbitrary projected image is Λ-flat. The converse uses the tame-level degeneracy count over all divisors of N₀, as in Corollary3.7’s proof.
Prop 3.4: Λ_K ⊆ 𝒦 and X is transcendental over the algebraic closure M of ℚ_p in 𝒦, so [M : K] divides [𝒦 : L].
acceptance: The non-primitive part of h^ord ⊗ L need not be semisimple (oldforms with repeated U_ℓ-eigenvalues), which is why the statement is for primitive components; L1/reduced-hida-algebra removes the U_ℓ to obtain a reduced algebra.

sources.locator: §3, Proposition 3.4, Theorem 3.5 and the terminology before them, pp. 251–252; Theorem 3.6 and Corollary 3.7, p. 253; §6, proof of Corollary3.7, pp.264–265 (Numdam printed pagination)
sources.match: Primitive components of the ordinary Hecke algebra over the fraction field of Λ_K, their fields of definition, and the exact count of ordinary forms of each weight k ≥ 2 belonging to a primitive cuspidal component.

nodes.title: Nakayama's lemma for compact modules over complete local rings
nodes.statement: Let Λ be complete noetherian local with maximal ideal 𝔪 and finite residue field. Let M be a profinite Hausdorff Λ-module with continuous action and a basis of open Λ-submodules. Then ⋂_n 𝔪ⁿM=0 and the canonical map M→lim_n M/𝔪ⁿM is an algebraic isomorphism (equip each quotient with its quotient topology to obtain the topological statement). If M/𝔪M is finite, lifts of any finite generating set generate M over Λ.
hypotheses: M is profinite with continuous Λ-action and a basis of open Λ-submodules. Before finite generation is proved, the submodules 𝔪ⁿM need not be open.
proofSteps: Each finite continuous quotient M/U is killed by some power of 𝔪; hence for every open Λ-submodule U, some 𝔪ⁿM is contained in U. This proves separation. Each 𝔪ⁿ is finitely generated, so 𝔪ⁿM is a compact image of a finite power of M and is closed. Nested compact cosets prove surjectivity to the inverse limit.

Let N be generated by finitely many lifts of generators modulo 𝔪. It is the image of compact Λ^r and is closed. Iterating M=N+𝔪M gives M=N+𝔪ⁿM. For every open U, therefore M=N+U; closedness of N yields M=N.
acceptance: This replaces the earlier citation of NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa NE.0, a roadmap outside the upstream order; the lemma moves down here.

sources.match: Finiteness of the ordinary Hecke algebra over Λ is deduced from finiteness modulo the maximal ideal by Nakayama's lemma for compact Λ-modules.

nodes.title: Hida's ordinary projector on definite quaternionic forms
nodes.statement: F is a totally real field of even degree d, p an odd prime, D/F the quaternion algebra ramified exactly at the infinite places, X(U) = D^×\G^D(A_f)/U for open compact U ⊆ GL₂(𝒪_F ⊗ Ẑ) with U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) for v | p, U_a = U ∩ U(p^a) and U⁰_a = U ∩ U₀(p^a), and 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension K of ℚ_p. For an 𝒪-module R, H⁰(X(U_a), R) is the module of R-valued functions on the finite set X(U_a), with the Hecke operators T₀(p) = [U_a (1 0; 0 ϖ_p) U_a] (ϖ_p a finite idele with a uniformiser at each v | p and 1 elsewhere), T₀(𝔭_i) for the primes above p, the group G(U_a) and T(ℓ), S(ℓ) for ℓ ∤ p with U_ℓ maximal. For R finite as a set, e := lim_n T₀(p)^{n!} is the finite ordinary projector of L0a; for R = 𝒪 it is the adic projector on the finite free module H⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪); for R = K/𝒪 it is the colimit of the projectors on the 𝒪/πⁿ-coefficients. e is an idempotent commuting with the Hecke algebra T(U_a, 𝒪), with change of coefficients R → R′, and with pullback and trace between levels U_b ⊆ U_a.
hypotheses: F even degree, p odd, D definite and unramified at all finite places.

Use p-power level a≥1 for the U-type operators and the assertion that the norm-form/constant subspace is killed by the ordinary projector. At maximal p-level a=0, T_p on constants instead has eigenvalue Np+1, a p-adic unit.
Supply finiteness in the unquotiented X(U) convention, as requested from R18.3; the central quotient in its existing definite-class-set statement is different.
proofSteps: The unquotiented X(U_a) must be finite. R18.3/definite-class-set establishes finiteness after quotienting additionally by A_f×. Request the precise finite-ray-class fibre comparison for the centre and level units, or an independent proof of finiteness in Skinner–Wiles’s convention. Conditional on that input, H⁰(X(U_a),R) is finite for finite R and finite free for R=𝒪. Do not identify the two class sets.
Apply L0a/finite-ordinary-projector and L0a/adic-instance; the projector for K/𝒪 is the colimit by naturality (L0a/ordinary-projector-natural).

Commutation with the Hecke algebra and with the level maps: these are 𝒪-linear and commute with T₀(p) (Skinner–Wiles's computation of double cosets), so they commute with every power and with the limit.
acceptance: Moved down from OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.1 (tier 20) to this tier-16 layer, as the upstream order requires; R21.1 imports it from here.

nodes.title: The nearly ordinary Hecke algebra T_∞(U, 𝒪)
nodes.statement: F is a totally real field of even degree d, p an odd prime, D/F the quaternion algebra ramified exactly at the infinite places, X(U) = D^×\G^D(A_f)/U for open compact U ⊆ GL₂(𝒪_F ⊗ Ẑ) with U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) for v | p, U_a = U ∩ U(p^a) and U⁰_a = U ∩ U₀(p^a), and 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension K of ℚ_p. Let T(U_a, 𝒪) ⊆ End_𝒪(H⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)) be generated by T₀(p), the T₀(𝔭_i), G(U_a) and T(ℓ), S(ℓ) for ℓ ∤ p with U_ℓ maximal, and T₂(U_a, 𝒪) := eT(U_a, 𝒪), its image in End_𝒪(eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)). The transition maps T₂(U_b, 𝒪) → T₂(U_a, 𝒪) (b ≥ a) are surjective and T_∞(U, 𝒪) := lim_a T₂(U_a, 𝒪). With G(U) = lim_a G(U_a) ≅ (𝒪_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× × Z(U) there is a continuous map 𝒪[[G(U)]] → T_∞(U, 𝒪), making T_∞(U, 𝒪) an algebra over the weight algebra Λ′_𝒪 of L5/totally-real-weight-algebra.
hypotheses: As in L5/quaternionic-ordinary-projector.
proofSteps: The transition maps are restrictions of Hecke operators along the pullback maps, which are compatible with e; surjectivity holds because generators map to generators.
The G(U_a) act through the diamond-type operators, compatible in a, giving 𝒪[[G(U)]] → T_∞(U, 𝒪) by the universal property of the completed group ring (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1).

By the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence for definite quaternion algebras (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3), T₂(U_a, 𝒪) is Skinner–Wiles's Hecke algebra eT*₂(U_a, 𝒪) of Hilbert cusp forms of parallel weight two.
acceptance: Moved down from OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.1.
