nodes.title: The ordinary part does not grow in Γ₀(p^a)-level
nodes.statement: F is a totally real field of even degree d, p an odd prime, D/F the quaternion algebra ramified exactly at the infinite places, X(U) = D^×\G^D(A_f)/U for open compact U ⊆ GL₂(𝒪_F ⊗ Ẑ) with U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) for v | p, U_a = U ∩ U(p^a) and U⁰_a = U ∩ U₀(p^a), and 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension K of ℚ_p. For a ≥ 2 the double coset U⁰_a (1 0; 0 ϖ_p) U⁰_a equals U⁰_a (1 0; 0 ϖ_p) U⁰_{a−1}, so T₀(p) maps H⁰(X(U⁰_a), K/𝒪) into the image of H⁰(X(U⁰_{a−1}), K/𝒪), and eH⁰(X(U⁰_a), K/𝒪) = eH⁰(X(U⁰_1), K/𝒪). Moreover H⁰(X(U⁰_a), K/𝒪) = H⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪)^{G(U_a)}.
hypotheses: As in L5/quaternionic-ordinary-projector.
proofSteps: The double coset identity is a matrix computation at the places above p.

Iterating, the image of T₀(p)^{a−1} lies in the level-U⁰_1 forms, and e is a limit of powers of T₀(p) on which T₀(p) is invertible, so the ordinary part is contained in, hence equal to, the level-U⁰_1 ordinary part.
Invariants: U⁰_a/U_a ≅ G(U_a)-part acting on X(U_a).
acceptance: Moved down from OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.1.

sources.locator: §3.2, proof of Proposition 3.3, p. 36 (Numdam PDF page 33)
sources.match: The double coset identity and the resulting independence of the ordinary part from the Γ₀(p^a)-level, and the identification of U⁰_a-invariants with G(U_a)-invariants.

nodes.title: Pontryagin duality for the ordinary quaternionic towers
nodes.statement: F is a totally real field of even degree d, p an odd prime, D/F the quaternion algebra ramified exactly at the infinite places, X(U) = D^×\G^D(A_f)/U for open compact U ⊆ GL₂(𝒪_F ⊗ Ẑ) with U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) for v | p, U_a = U ∩ U(p^a) and U⁰_a = U ∩ U₀(p^a), and 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension K of ℚ_p. Put H_∞(U) = lim_→ eH⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪) and H⁺_∞(U) = lim_→ eH⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪)⁺ along pullbacks, and M_∞(U) = lim_← eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)⁺, M⁺_∞(U) = lim_← eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪) along traces (the superscript + keeps the underlying module and changes the Hecke action to the adjoint action of Skinner–Wiles, p.34; the norm-form subspace is a separate object killed by e at positive p-power level). These are T_∞(U, 𝒪)-modules, and the perfect pairings at finite level induce T_∞(U, 𝒪)-isomorphisms M_∞(U) ≅ Hom_𝒪(H_∞(U), K/𝒪) and M⁺_∞(U) ≅ Hom_𝒪(H⁺_∞(U), K/𝒪).
hypotheses: As in L5/quaternionic-ordinary-projector.

Pass to the cofinal levels at which stabilizer orders are units (in particular to free/neat levels), as required for the perfect integral pairing. The + notation denotes the adjoint Hecke module, not a subspace.
proofSteps: The pairing on functions on X(U_a) weighted by the stabiliser orders c_{U_a}(x) is perfect over 𝒪 when the stabilisers are trivial, which holds for a large (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3, integral pairing and neat level).

For the stabilizer-weighted finite-level pairing, t acting on one side is adjoint to t^adjoint on the other; hence the + action makes the duality Hecke-linear. Pullback is adjoint to trace and e is compatible with adjoints. Passing to the cofinal perfect-pairing levels identifies the discrete direct-limit tower with the continuous dual of the compact inverse-limit tower. The algebraic CharacterModule baseline alone does not supply topological Pontryagin duality.

The pinned CharacterModule is algebraic Hom(A,ℚ/ℤ), not a topological Pontryagin dual. Finite-level character functions are continuous automatically. For the inverse/direct limits use the continuous duality interface of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0 with its compact/discrete topology; no character-module declaration alone supplies this passage.
acceptance: Moved down from OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.1.

sources.match: The ordinary towers H_∞, M_∞ and their ± variants, the stabiliser-weighted pairings and the Pontryagin duality between the towers.

nodes.title: Λ-adic Hilbert modular forms and their ordinary parts
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, p odd, E/ℚ_p finite with ring of integers 𝒪_E, Λ = 𝒪_E[[T]], u a topological generator of 1 + pℤ_p and ν_k : Λ → 𝒪_E, T ↦ u^{k−1} − 1, the weight-k specialisation. For a totally odd narrow ray class character χ of conductor 𝔫 prime to p, a Λ-adic Hilbert modular form of tame level 𝔫 and character χ is a family F = (c(𝔞, F))_𝔞 ∈ Λ^{integral ideals} together with constant terms, such that for every integer k ≥ 2 the specialisation ν_k(F) is the q-expansion of a classical Hilbert modular form of parallel weight k, level 𝔫p and character χω^{1−k}. They form a Λ-module M(𝔫, χ) with cuspidal submodule S(𝔫, χ), Hecke operators T_𝔩 (𝔩 ∤ 𝔫p) and U_𝔩 (𝔩 | 𝔫p). The ordinary projector e = lim_n (∏_{𝔭|p} U_𝔭)^{n!} defines the Hida families M°(𝔫, χ) = eM(𝔫, χ) and S°(𝔫, χ) = eS(𝔫, χ), finite free over Λ conditional on the separate parallel-weight Hida–Wiles construction/control input, with Hecke algebras T̃ and T acting on them.
hypotheses: F totally real; p odd; χ totally odd of conductor 𝔫 prime to p, with values in E; parallel weights. Finite freeness/control is the Hida–Wiles input restated in DKV, not proved by the coefficient-family definition or by the definite quaternionic control theorem alone.
proofSteps: Define the coefficient-family module and its Hecke action. Construct the integral ordinary projector using the finite-quotient hypotheses. To obtain finite freeness and classical ordinary control in all totally real degrees, import the separate parallel-weight Hida–Wiles construction; DKV §3.1 restates this input, and the definite even-degree quaternionic control theorem does not prove it for arbitrary F.

The q-expansion principle for p-adic Hilbert modular forms on the ordinary Igusa tower makes 'a family of q-expansions specialising to classical forms' a module of p-adic modular forms (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T5, as red-team finding RT-AREA-langlands-1/8 requires, not IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.1).
acceptance: Weight-one specialisation ν_1 is not required to be classical in the definition; Dasgupta–Kakde–Ventullo study it separately.

nodes.title: A Hida family is determined by its Fourier expansion
nodes.statement: Let Λ_{(1)} = 𝒪_E[[T]]_{(T)} be the localisation of Λ at the weight-one prime (T) (a discrete valuation ring in which p is invertible). The map c : S°(𝔫, χ)_{(1)} → ∏_{𝔞 ⊆ 𝒪_F} Λ_{(1)}, H ↦ (c(𝔞, H))_𝔞, sending a cuspidal Hida family to its normalised Fourier coefficients, is injective and Λ_{(1)}-linear.
hypotheses: χ of conductor 𝔫 prime to p; cuspidal families.
χ totally odd as in L5/lambda-adic-hilbert-forms.
proofSteps: A Λ-adic form is by definition a family of coefficients; the Fourier expansion map is injective on S(𝔫, χ) because a cuspidal Hilbert form is determined by its normalised coefficients c(𝔞, ·) (its constant terms vanish), so a family all of whose coefficients vanish specialises to zero at every k ≥ 2, hence is zero.

For H=f/s, s∉(T), whose coefficients vanish in each Λ_(T), injectivity of Λ→Λ_(T) implies every coefficient of f is zero. Hence f=0 by the coefficient-family definition and H=0. This common-denominator argument proves the stated map into the infinite product; flat localization need not commute with arbitrary products.
acceptance: The paper uses this without proof; it is one of the three facts the maintainer assigned to this layer.

sources.match: A Hida family is determined by its Fourier expansion: the canonical injective Λ_{(1)}-linear map from S°(𝔫, χ)_{(1)} to the product of copies of Λ_{(1)} indexed by integral ideals.

nodes.title: The localised cuspidal Hecke algebra is reduced at minimal tame level
nodes.statement: Let 𝔪 ⊆ T be the height-one prime of the cuspidal Hecke algebra generated by T, T_𝔩 − (1 + χε(𝔩)) for 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫p and U_𝔩 − 1 for 𝔩 | 𝔫p (the Eisenstein prime through E₁(1, χ_S)). If the tame character χ has conductor equal to the tame level 𝔫, then the localisation T_{(𝔪)} is reduced: there are no 𝔫-old forms, so T_{(𝔪)} ⊗ Frac(Λ) is a product of fields.
hypotheses: cond(χ) = 𝔫; the localisation at the height-one prime 𝔪.
χ totally odd. Supply parallel-weight ordinary control and the full minimal-tame-level newform semisimplicity input credited to Hida by DKV p.857; it is a recorded gap.
proofSteps: At tame level cond(χ)=𝔫 all classical constituents are tame-new. Use the ordinary newform/control input including tame U_𝔩 and the selected ordinary U_𝔭 eigenvalues. Normality of T_𝔩 away from 𝔫p alone proves neither bad-prime semisimplicity nor reducedness of their enlarged image.

Under that input, arithmetic specialization and multiplicity one give a reduced generic full Hecke image. The family image is Λ-torsion-free as a submodule of endomorphisms of the finite free ordinary module, hence embeds into the generic image; localizing at 𝔪 preserves reducedness. The primary Hida argument remains explicitly imported.
acceptance: The hypothesis cond(χ) = 𝔫 is essential: with old forms at a prime 𝔩 | 𝔫, U_𝔩 has repeated eigenvalues on oldspaces and the Hecke algebra including U_𝔩 can contain nilpotents.

sources.match: Since the conductor of χ equals the tame level there are no 𝔫-old forms, so T_{(𝔪)} is reduced; the paper credits the observation to Hida and refers to Hida's proof of Theorem 3.6 and Corollary 3.7.

nodes.title: The total ring of fractions of the localised Hecke algebra and its eigenfamilies
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of L5/hilbert-hecke-reduced, let L = Frac(T_{(𝔪)}) be the total ring of fractions. Then T_{(𝔪)} ↪ L and L ≅ ∏_{i=1}^t L_{H_i}, a finite product of fields, each a finite extension of Frac(Λ) corresponding to a cuspidal Hida eigenfamily H_i; the image of T_𝔞 in L_{H_i} is the normalised coefficient c(𝔞, H_i). These coefficients generate a finite local Λ-subalgebra Λ_{H_i} ⊆ L_{H_i}, the image of T_{(𝔪)} in L_{H_i} is the localisation of Λ_{H_i} at a height-one prime 𝔪_{H_i} over (T), and c(𝔩, H_i) ≡ 1 + χ(𝔩) mod 𝔪_{H_i} for 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫p and c(𝔩, H_i) ≡ 1 mod 𝔪_{H_i} for 𝔩 | 𝔫p: each H_i specialises at 𝔪_{H_i} to the weight-one form E₁(1, χ_S).
hypotheses: As in L5/hilbert-hecke-reduced.

Supply the finite ordinary-module/control and full Hecke reducedness inputs of L5/lambda-adic-hilbert-forms and hilbert-hecke-reduced. The algebraic total-quotient-ring step is routine once the finite reduced Hecke algebra is available.
proofSteps: A reduced Noetherian ring has finitely many minimal primes; localizing at all nonzerodivisors gives the product of the fraction fields of its minimal-prime quotients. The pinned Mathlib FractionRing is precisely this total quotient localization for any commutative ring, although it has a field instance only under domain hypotheses. For this finite torsion-free Λ-algebra the factors are finite over Frac(Λ).

The minimal primes of T_{(𝔪)} correspond to the Hecke eigensystems in S°(𝔫, χ) ⊗ Frac(Λ)ᵃˡᵍ that specialise into 𝔪, i.e. to cuspidal Hida eigenfamilies; the field of each is generated over Frac(Λ) by its coefficients.
The congruences are the description of 𝔪 by its generators.
acceptance: Each eigenfamily H_i specialises at 𝔪_{H_i} to E₁(1, χ_S), as the congruences (51) state.

nodes.title: Hida's big Galois representation and its nearly ordinary twist
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3, Γ = Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ) for the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension and Γ′ the diamond group of the tower Y₁(p^t), both identified with 1 + pℤ_p. For a branch of the ordinary Hecke algebra with coefficient ring H^ord_F (a local domain finite flat over ℤ_p[[Γ′]], attached to a Λ-adic eigen newform F), there is a finitely generated torsion-free H^ord_F-module T^ord of generic rank two with a continuous G_ℚ-action, unramified outside a finite set S ∋ p, ∞, with Frobenius polynomials in Ochiai’s cohomological convention. This convention must be identified with the EPW Hecke representation by the appropriate dual and Tate twist; a bare trace(Frob_ℓ)=T_ℓ identification with the EPW representation is not asserted. The nearly ordinary Hecke algebra is H^{n.o.}_F := H^ord_F ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} ℤ_p[[Γ]] ≅ H^ord_F[[Γ]], and the nearly ordinary deformation is T := T^ord ⊗̂ ℤ_p[[Γ]](χ̃) ⊗ ωⁱ, with χ̃ : G_ℚ ↠ Γ ⊂ ℤ_p[[Γ]]^× the universal cyclotomic character. Under (F), T is free of rank two with irreducible residual representation. Its determinant is χ⁻¹χ̃²χ̃′⁻¹ω^{2i}, up to the finite-order branch character. At an arithmetic point κ of weight w(κ) and 1≤j≤w(κ)+1, specialization along χ^{j−1}∘κ is T_{f_κ}⊗χ^j⊗ωⁱ, using the cohomological Deligne lattice of weight w(κ)+2. All formulas for the untwisted deformation explicitly set i=0.
hypotheses: p ≥ 3; a branch H^ord_F of the ordinary Hecke algebra; hypothesis (F) for the freeness statements.

Use Ochiai §1, pp.114–115: geometric Frobenius, the cohomological T_{f_κ}, and the indicated universal twists. An arithmetic pair (j,κ) specializes T to T_{f_κ}⊗χ^j⊗ωⁱ; even the trivial Γ-specialization j=1 includes one cyclotomic twist. The bridge to the L1/EPW convention is an explicit missing input.
proofSteps: The ordinary parts of the p-adic Tate modules of J₁(Np^t) (ModularCurvesPartII R14.2) form a projective system of H^ord-modules with Galois action; their limit, localised at the branch, is T^ord (Hida's construction; equivalently, the Galois action on the family symbol module of L1 through the comparison of étale and Betti homology).

The trace and determinant identities hold at the Zariski-dense set of weight-two points by the Eichler–Shimura relation (ModularCurvesPartII R14.6) and extend by continuity; equivalently, the trace determinant is obtained by interpolating the determinants of the classical points through finite quotients (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.4).

Specialisation at an arithmetic point of weight w(κ) + 2 is Deligne's representation by Hida's control theorem (L0/hida-control-theorem) and the Eichler–Shimura comparison at weight w(κ) + 2 through L1's family symbols.
acceptance: This is the rational (F = ℚ) ordinary big Galois representation; RS-08 named OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.3 as owner, but R21.3 is in tier 20 and plans the totally real nearly ordinary representation of Skinner–Wiles; the rational construction moves down here, and R21.3 imports it for F = ℚ.

nodes.title: The ordinary filtration of the big Galois representation at p
nodes.statement: Under (F), the restriction of T to a decomposition group G_{ℚ_p} has a filtration 0 → F⁺T → T → F⁻T → 0 by H^{n.o.}_F-submodules free of rank one, with F⁺T ≅ ℤ_p[[Γ]](χ̃) ⊗̂ H^ord_F(α̃) ⊗ ωⁱ where α̃ : G_{ℚ_p} → (H^ord_F)^× is unramified with α̃(Frob_p) = A_p and κ(A_p) = a_p(f_κ) at every arithmetic point; the character of F⁻T is det(T)/char(F⁺T), namely χ⁻¹χ̃χ̃′⁻¹α̃⁻¹ωⁱ up to the finite-order character occurring in det(T). The filtration specialises at every arithmetic point to the ordinary filtration of T_{f_κ} ⊗ χ^j ⊗ ωⁱ, and is saturated (the quotient F⁻T is torsion-free).
hypotheses: Hypothesis (F); p-distinguished residual representation for uniqueness of the filtration.

The Hida–Wiles ordinary-line theorem supplies integral free rank-one F⁺ and F⁻ in Ochiai’s normalization. Freeness of T and residual irreducibility alone do not prove this local filtration. In the cohomological convention the unramified α̃-line is the submodule before the universal cyclotomic twist; the usual connected–étale quotient must first be dualized appropriately.
proofSteps: Apply the Hida–Wiles ordinary-filtration input in Ochiai’s cohomological convention (§1, pp.115–116), retaining its integral lattice and rank-one freeness hypotheses. A connected–étale decomposition with an unramified quotient in the opposite convention cannot be substituted without the normalization bridge.

The rank-one integral submodule and quotient are part of the Hida–Wiles ordinary-filtration input, recalled as properties4–5 by Ochiai. They are not consequences of global freeness or residual irreducibility alone. Identify the unramified α̃ character via the ordinary p-divisible-group theorem requested from R14.6; its existing ℓ≠p semistable-Tate statement is not this theorem.
Specialisation compatibility follows from the uniqueness of the ordinary filtration of a p-distinguished representation.

In a basis respecting the filtration, determinant is the product of the two diagonal characters. Hence char(F⁻T)=det(T)/char(F⁺T). This also checks each arithmetic specialization and the required Tate twist.
acceptance: The ordinary p-divisible-group and integral ordinary-line input is requested as an extension of ModularCurvesPartII R14.6. Its existing semistable ℓ≠p Tate interface does not supply it; this node is conditional on that extension and the Hida–Wiles input.

nodes.title: Greenberg and Bloch–Kato Selmer groups of the nearly ordinary deformation
nodes.statement: Let A = T ⊗_{H^{n.o.}} Hom_{ℤ_p,cont}(H^{n.o.}_F, ℚ_p/ℤ_p) be the discrete module attached to T and ℚ_S the maximal extension unramified outside S. For a local condition H¹_?(ℚ_p, A) ⊆ H¹(ℚ_p, A), Sel_?(T) is the kernel of H¹(ℚ_S/ℚ, A) → ∏_{ℓ∈S, ℓ≠p} H¹(ℚ_ℓ, A)/H¹_ur(ℚ_ℓ, A) × H¹(ℚ_p, A)/H¹_?(ℚ_p, A). Greenberg's condition is H¹_Gr = ker(H¹(ℚ_p, A) → H¹(ℚ_p^ur, F⁻A)); the Bloch–Kato condition is the limit of the Bloch–Kato finite parts H¹_f on the Φ_{s,t}^{(j,k)}-torsion of A along the height-two ideals of arithmetic points. Under (F): Sel_BK(T) = Sel_Gr(T), independent of (j, k), and its Pontryagin dual is a finitely generated torsion H^{n.o.}_F-module.
hypotheses: Hypothesis (F).

The BK=Greenberg comparison and cotorsion assertion are Ochiai Proposition A, pp.116–117, whose primary proof in Ochiai 2003 remains the recorded input. Arithmetic control retains global invariants, local inertia and localization-cokernel errors; their finite/bounded vanishing is an additional hypothesis, particularly at exceptional ordinary points.
proofSteps: The Greenberg condition is SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2's Greenberg local condition for the filtration of L4/ordinary-filtration; Selmer groups and their duals are L2's constructions over the coefficient ring H^{n.o.}_F.

Equality of the two Selmer groups: at each arithmetic specialisation the ordinary Greenberg condition agrees with the Bloch–Kato finite condition up to finite error controlled uniformly (Ochiai, A generalization of the Coleman map, §4); pass to the limit.
Torsionness: specialise to a weight and use Kato's cyclotomic theorem (KatoEulerSystems L4) and the control theorem for Selmer groups (SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3).

For arithmetic control apply the supplier’s kernel-control exact sequence to the actual localization image, not automatically the full local-condition quotient. Ordinary direct-summand freeness does not kill inertia invariants or exceptional Euler factors.
acceptance: Under (F) the dual Selmer group is torsion, which is what makes a characteristic ideal and a main conjecture meaningful.

nodes.title: The Selmer complex of the nearly ordinary deformation
nodes.statement: With specified Greenberg and unramified local maps, form the Selmer fibre complex over H=H^{n.o.}_F. It is perfect only under the imported cochain/local-condition perfectness hypotheses. Its H¹ is the extended compact Selmer module, with the local H⁰ terms in its comparison to the classical compact Selmer group. For an arithmetic quotient H→H/𝔓, ambient derived base change gives a comparison whose cone is the sum of the local-condition comparison cones; it is an isomorphism only when these vanish. If H is a normal domain, this complex is perfect and generically acyclic, its inverse determinant has height-one divisor Σ_i(−1)^i length H^i; identifying that divisor with the dual classical Selmer characteristic ideal also requires the stated local-error and other-cohomology comparisons.
hypotheses: (F); explicit local maps of complexes and their specialization comparisons. Supply perfectness over the actual possibly nonregular H, ambient derived base change, and the local correction-cone computations. Supply normality, generic acyclicity and the cohomology/duality comparisons for a scalar determinant formula. These extra conditions are not consequences of (F).
proofSteps: Apply the lower-tier Selmer fibre construction to the actual local maps. Its long exact sequence retains local H⁰ terms, so H¹ need not equal the classical compact Selmer kernel.

Tensor the fibre diagram in the derived category and use SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/derived-control and correction-complex. The local comparison cones remain; F⁺ being a direct summand over H does not make inertia cohomology commute with specialization.

Once perfectness and generic acyclicity are proved, apply the supplier’s inverse determinant formula. Its divisor is the alternating cohomology-length sum. Specialize to a classical dual-Selmer characteristic ideal only after proving that the additional cohomology and local error divisors vanish or retaining them as factors.
acceptance: The stage asks for the family Selmer complex 'through R07', now SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3; only the instance is planned here.

nodes.title: Beilinson–Kato classes in Hida families
nodes.statement: Under (F), let R be the set of square-free integers prime to S. There is a family Z(r) ∈ H¹(ℚ(ζ_r), T*(1)), r ∈ R, unramified outside the primes above S, with the Euler system norm relations Norm_{ℚ(ζ_{rq})/ℚ(ζ_r)} Z(rq) = P_q(Frob_q) Z(r) for primes q ∉ S with q ∤ r, where P_q(X) = det(1 − Frob_q X | T) ∈ H^{n.o.}_F[X] and Frob_q is a geometric Frobenius. For every arithmetic point κ and 1 ≤ j ≤ w(κ) + 1, the specialisation z_{(j,κ)}(1) of Z(1) is Kato's zeta element for f_κ twisted by χ^jωⁱ, and the dual exponential of its image in H¹_{/f}(ℚ_p, T_{(j,κ)}*(1)) equals L^{(p)}(f*_κ, ω^{i−j}, j)/((2π√−1)^{j−1} C^{(−1)^i}_{∞,κ}) · δ^{dR}_κ, with L^{(p)} the L-function without its Euler factor at p and C^±_{∞,κ} complex periods.
hypotheses: Hypothesis (F); p ≥ 3.
proofSteps: At each level Np^t and each cyclotomic level, Kato's zeta elements of KatoEulerSystems L2 lie in the étale cohomology of the modular curves; their ordinary projections are compatible under the trace maps in the weight (via the moment maps, KatoEulerSystems L1) and in the cyclotomic variable (KatoEulerSystems L2 norm relations).
The limit over both towers defines Z(r) in Iwasawa cohomology of T*(1); the norm relations are inherited.
The dual-exponential formula at arithmetic points is Kato's explicit reciprocity law (KatoEulerSystems L3) at the specialised form.
acceptance: At every arithmetic point the dual exponential of the specialised class is the critical L-value over the complex period (Proposition 1.2(3)).

sources.locator: §1, Proposition 1.2 with the de Rham conventions before it, pp. 117–118
sources.match: The Beilinson–Kato elements Z(r) for the nearly ordinary deformation, their norm relations with the Euler factors P_q, and the interpolation of Kato's dual exponential formula at every arithmetic point.

nodes.title: The Perrin-Riou big logarithm in families
nodes.statement: Let M be an unramified profinite ℤ_p[G_{ℚ_p}]-module (for example the unramified twist of F⁻T*(1) attached to a Hida family) and D(M) = (M ⊗̂ ℤ_p^{ur})^{G_{ℚ_p}} with Frobenius φ. There is a map L_M : H¹(ℚ_p, M ⊗̂ Λ_Γ(−j_univ)) → D(M) ⊗̂ I^{−1}Λ_Γ, where I is the kernel of specialisation at j = −1, functorial in M and commuting with End_{ℤ_p[G_{ℚ_p}]}(M), with kernel H⁰(ℚ_p, M) and image under the pole-residue quotient I⁻¹Λ_Γ/Λ_Γ contained in D(M)^{φ=1}; for M finite free over ℤ_p it is Perrin-Riou's big logarithm. The application to the suitable unramified quotient of T*(1), after removing its universal cyclotomic twist, is a regulator. Identifying it with Ochiai’s map Ξ:H¹_{/f}(ℚ_p,T*(1))→Frac(H^{n.o.}_F), with his normalization, integrality and height-one length comparison, is a separate input; it does not follow from KLZ Theorem8.2.3 alone.
hypotheses: M unramified and profinite; Hida-family coefficients for the application.

j_univ denotes the universal cyclotomic character, not an integer. Use the quotient of the Tate dual induced by the dual of F⁺T, rather than ambiguously dualizing F⁻. Frobenius on D(M) has the KLZ unramified-coefficient convention. The residue is in I⁻¹Λ/Λ, not Λ/I.
proofSteps: Define N(M) = D(M)[[π]] with φ and its left inverse ψ, use Fontaine's isomorphism H¹(ℚ_p, M ⊗ Λ_Γ(−j)) ≅ (π⁻¹N(M))^{ψ=1} and the exact sequence for 1 − φ; φ is invertible on D(M), so N(M)^{ψ=0} = D(M) ⊗̂ Λ_Γ.
Both sides commute with inverse limits, so the case of finite M suffices.
acceptance: The KLZ unramified profinite-module regulator is planned here in its stated scope. Ochiai’s Ξ and the integral normalization/length comparison remain separate source inputs; the KLZ pole and H⁰-kernel prevent an automatic integral height-one isomorphism.

sources.locator: §8.2, Definition 8.2.1 and Theorem 8.2.3 with proof, p. 42 (arXiv v6)

nodes.title: The two-variable p-adic L-function of a Hida family and the family reciprocity law
nodes.statement: Under (F), set L_p(T) := Ξ(loc_{/f}(Z(1))) ∈ Frac(H^{n.o.}_F), integral when H^{n.o.}_F is integrally closed. Assume H^{n.o.}_F is normal for the following length/valuation assertion. Then (1) for every height-one prime 𝔭 of H^{n.o.}_F, length_{(H^{n.o.})_𝔭} (H¹_{/f}(ℚ_p, T*(1))/loc_{/f}(Z(1)))_𝔭 = ord_𝔭(L_p(T)); (2) for every arithmetic (j, κ) with 0 ≤ j − 1 ≤ w(κ), (χ^{j−1} ∘ κ)(L_p(T))/C_{p,κ} equals (−1)^{j−1}(j − 1)!·(1 − ω^{i−j}(p)p^{j−1}/a_p(f_κ))·(p^{j−1}/a_p(f_κ))^{q(i,j)}·G(ω^{j−i})·L(f_κ, ω^{i−j}, j)/((2π√−1)^{j−1}C^{(−1)^i}_{∞,κ}), with C_{p,κ} a p-adic period, G a Gauss sum and q(i, j) the p-order of the conductor of ω^{i−j}. The interpolation is derived from Kato's reciprocity law at each arithmetic point, not imposed as a definition, The comparison with L1’s Mazur–Kitagawa function is conditional on an integral analytic period identification; dense pointwise interpolation alone does not give a unit ratio on the branch.
hypotheses: (F); Ochiai’s normalized Ξ and Theorem B input, which are not consequences of the abstract KLZ regulator. H^{n.o.}_F normal for integrality and the height-one DVR length formula. For the branch-unit comparison, an integral analytic identification of the two period lattices.
proofSteps: (2): specialise Ξ at (j, κ), where it becomes the Bloch–Kato dual exponential with the Euler-like factor (L4/family-big-logarithm), and apply the dual-exponential formula of L4/big-beilinson-kato-classes.

For the length equality use Ochiai Theorem B, p.119, under normality. Its primary Coleman-map construction is a recorded gap. A rank-one local Euler-characteristic calculation and unramified quotient do not by themselves prove that a generic Perrin-Riou regulator is injective with pseudo-null cokernel.

Compare the integral family period lattices and regulator normalizations first. If this gives a branch-unit change of trivialization, L1/period-change-of-trivialisation supplies the unit formula; then dense interpolation identifies the functions. Without that lattice comparison, the unit claim remains unresolved.
acceptance: The family reciprocity law is derived from the single-form reciprocity laws and the construction of Ξ, as the stage requires; it is not a definition of the family class.

sources.match: The two-variable p-adic L-function as the image of the local Beilinson–Kato class under Ξ, the length formula at height-one primes, the interpolation formula at arithmetic points, and the integrality caveat when H^{n.o.} is not normal.

nodes.title: Euler system divisibility for the nearly ordinary deformation
nodes.statement: Assume (F), that H^{n.o.}_F ≅ 𝒪[[X₁, X₂]] for the ring of integers 𝒪 of a finite extension of ℚ_p, and that there are τ ∈ G_{ℚ(μ_{p^∞})} acting on T by a unipotent matrix (1 P_τ; 0 1) with P_τ ≠ 0 and τ′ ∈ G_ℚ acting by −1. Then there is k ≥ 0 such that for every height-one prime 𝔭 of H^{n.o.}_F, length (Sel(T)^∨)_𝔭 ≤ length (H¹_{/f}(ℚ_p, T*(1))/loc_{/f}(Z(1)))_𝔭 + ord_𝔭(P_τ^k). Combined with L4/two-variable-l-function, (L_p(T)·P_τ^k) ⊆ char(Sel(T)^∨), equivalently a generator of char(Sel(T)^∨) divides L_p(T)·P_τ^k: one divisibility of Greenberg's two-variable main conjecture for Hida families, up to the factor P_τ^k.
hypotheses: (F); H^{n.o.}_F a two-variable power series ring; the elements τ, τ′ as stated.
proofSteps: Ochiai's Euler system argument over the deformation ring: Kolyvagin derivative classes are built from Z(r) and controlled at height-two specialisations, where Kato–Rubin's cyclotomic bound applies; the bounds at a Zariski-dense set of height-two primes assemble to a bound at each height-one prime, the defect measured by P_τ.
The identification of the right-hand side with ord_𝔭 L_p(T) is L4/two-variable-l-function (1).

Use the height-one characteristic divisor over the regular ring 𝒪[[X₁,X₂]], of Krull dimension three. Do not apply the dimension-two Fitting=characteristic theorem of SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/selmer-fitting-characteristic to this ring.
acceptance: The hypotheses are visible: when H^{n.o.} is not regular, or no τ with nonzero P_τ exists, no bound is asserted.

sources.locator: §1, Theorem C and the final Theorem, pp. 120–121; §2, Theorems 2.4 and 2.6
sources.match: The Euler system bound for Galois deformations over a two-variable power series ring under the existence of τ and τ′, and the resulting inequality towards the two-variable main conjecture.

nodes.title: Triangulations and the regulator over Coleman families
nodes.statement: Let f_α be a noble refined eigenform (p-regular and a noncritical refinement) of weight k + 2 and F the Coleman family through it over an affinoid disc V of weight space (PadicFamilies L2), with Galois representation M_V(F)* over O(V). After shrinking V: (1) the (φ, Γ)-module D†_rig(M_V(F)*) over the Robba ring over O(V) admits a canonical triangulation 0 → F⁺D → D → F⁻D → 0 with F⁻D ≅ R_{O(V)}(α_F⁻¹) and F⁺D a rank-one module given by α_F·ε_F(p)⁻¹ twisted by 1 + κ_V; (2) there is the Eichler–Shimura basis vector ω_F in (F⁻D_V(F)(1+κ_V+ε_F^(p)))^{Γ=1}, using D_V(F) rather than D_V(F)* as in LZ Theorem6.4.1 specialising at each classical weight t to the differential of f_t (Eichler–Shimura in families); (3) for A=O(V) reduced and α=α_F⁻¹ a unit with ‖α‖≤1 and α−1 a nonzerodivisor, LZ Proposition6.2.1 gives the injective single-family rank-one regulator L_{A,α}:H¹_Iw(ℚ_{p,∞},R_A(α))→A ⊗̂ O(𝒲), with its stated classical interpolation. The Rankin two-family quotient regulator and reciprocity of §7.1 require their additional second-family and tensor-quotient inputs. No constant-dimension crystalline module over the whole eigencurve neighbourhood is asserted: the triangulation exists only after shrinking around a noble point.
hypotheses: f_α noble; V a sufficiently small affinoid disc around its weight.

Noble means p-regular and noncritical refinement (LZ Definition4.6.3); a critical-slope nonsplit refinement can be noble. For the single-family regulator impose A reduced, α a unit of norm≤1, and α−1 a nonzerodivisor as in Proposition6.2.1. Keep the dual/twist conventions of Theorems6.3.2 and6.4.1 when pairing with ω_F.
proofSteps: Liu's triangulation theorem for families of refined trianguline representations gives (1) at a non-critical point, after shrinking V.
(2) is Andreatta–Iovita–Stevens's overconvergent Eichler–Shimura comparison composed with projection to F⁻ (Sen theory in families).

Apply LZ Proposition6.2.1, p.29, to the stated single rank-one R_A(α), checking α−1 is a nonzerodivisor. LZ Theorem7.1.4 instead constructs a regulator for the F⁻⁺ quotient of a Rankin pair of Coleman families; it is not a proof of the single-family assertion without those extra inputs. Its domain is H¹_Iw(ℚ_{p,∞},R_A(α))=R_A(α)^{ψ=1}, not ordinary H¹ at a single local field.
acceptance: The theorem is source-scoped as RS-08 requires: it covers Coleman families through noble points, with the triangulation hypothesis visible; the construction of Galois representations over the eigencurve and Liu's and Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao's theorems are imported as recorded inputs (gap 'Nonordinary family inputs').

sources.match: The Galois representation over a Coleman family through a noble eigenform, Liu's triangulation after shrinking, the Eichler–Shimura basis vector in families, and the family regulator and explicit reciprocity law for the Rankin–Eisenstein classes.
Definition of a noble refinement and the single-family rank-one regulator with the reduced-affinoid, norm and nonzerodivisor hypotheses.

nodes.title: Period modules of totally real Hida families
nodes.statement: In the setting of L5/ordinary-towers-duality, let 𝔪 be a maximal ideal of T_∞(U, 𝒪) and T_𝔪 the localisation. The period module of the family at 𝔪 is the T_𝔪-module P_𝔪 := M_∞(U)_𝔪 (and P⁺_𝔪 := M⁺_∞(U)_𝔪). It is faithful and finite over T_𝔪, and free over Λ′_𝒪 when U acts freely and the corrected L5/hida-freeness input is supplied. It is exported as an invertible T_𝔪-module, with trivialisations P_𝔪 ≅ T_𝔪 unique up to T_𝔪^×, only under the explicit hypothesis that P_𝔪 is free of rank one over T_𝔪 (a multiplicity-one statement, proved in the minimal case by Taylor–Wiles patching in OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting); without it P_𝔪 has generic rank one at each minimal prime of T_𝔪 whose classical specialisations are newforms of level exactly U, by multiplicity one for the definite quaternion algebra and strong multiplicity one, but need not be invertible. For F = ℚ (degree one, with the indefinite modular curve in place of the definite quaternion algebra) the corresponding object is L1's family period line, and the change-of-trivialisation formula is L1/period-change-of-trivialisation.
hypotheses: F of even degree; U acting freely for the Λ′-freeness; for invertibility, the hypothesis that P_𝔪 is free of rank one over T_𝔪.
Use L5/hida-freeness only after supplying its corrected finite-generation/projectivity input on every torsion-character factor; it is currently a gap.
proofSteps: Once the corrected finite-generation input is supplied, M_∞ is finite over the Hecke algebra and faithful by its image definition. For a finite module, annihilators localize; hence its localization at every maximal ideal is faithful and nonzero. Alternatively use the finite semilocal factor decomposition. Faithfulness without finite generation would not justify this step.

Generic rank one: at a minimal prime the dense weight-two specialisations (L5/algebraic-primes-dense) are quaternionic eigenforms whose eigenspaces in eH⁰(X(U_a), K) are one-dimensional when the corresponding Hilbert newform has level exactly U (Jacquet–Langlands and multiplicity one for D^×, HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3).
Invertibility: a finite faithful module that is free of rank one is invertible; trivialisations differ by units. No such statement is made without the hypothesis.
acceptance: The stage's condition is visible: invertibility is a hypothesis carried by the consumer (or proved by OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting), never asserted from Λ′-freeness alone.

sources.match: The modules M_∞(U), M⁺_∞(U) over T_∞(U, 𝒪), their Λ′-freeness, and the localisations at maximal ideals used for the deformation-theoretic comparison, where freeness over the Hecke algebra is proved separately.

Also (Mazur–Wiles): the ordinary part of the p-divisible group of J₁(Np^t) has, over the local ring at p, a connected–étale filtration whose étale quotient is unramified with Frob_p acting by U_p, compatibly in t; L4/ordinary-filtration passes it to the limit.

gaps.title: Coleman's overconvergent modular forms and Chenevier's comparison theorem
gaps.detail: The modular-symbol eigencurve C^± of L2 is planned from Bellaïche §3 without overconvergent forms. The comparison with the Coleman–Mazur–Buzzard eigencurve C (L2/coleman-mazur-comparison) needs Coleman's Banach modules of overconvergent modular forms with compact U_p and his control theorem (Coleman, Invent. Math. 124, 1996; Coleman–Mazur 1998, Internet Archive preprint, SHA-256 bf8e96f23fb3db2f886a5106547798c6d899941b316f340079b3aabb4ad04a70, §§7.1–7.5 read in R1-review) and Chenevier's comparison theorem for eigenvarieties (Chenevier, Duke Math. J. 126 (2005), Théorème 1, cited by Bellaïche Prop. 3.18). No roadmap plans Coleman's overconvergent elliptic modular forms (OverconvergentAutomorphicForms is perfectoid and Hilbert-based), and neither Coleman 1996 nor Chenevier 2005 was read. L3's uses of C (smoothness at decent points, Bellaïche Theorem 2.16) go through this comparison.

gaps.title: Dimension theorem narrowed; dense classical points still require separate inputs
gaps.detail: Buzzard Lemma 5.8 delegates equidimensionality to Chenevier Proposition 6.4.2. R1-review read that proposition with its proof (author copy glnfam.pdf, internal p. 53), Lemme 6.2.10 (pp. 47–48) and Lemme 6.4.3 (p. 54): the argument uses only that the Hecke image is a commutative subalgebra of End_A(N) for N finite projective over an equidimensional reduced affinoid A, so it applies in Buzzard's generality; the new node equidimensional-components (addedBy R1-review) records it. Remaining imports: Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces, results 2.1.5, 2.2.3, 2.2.7, 2.2.9 and 4.3.2, and Coleman–Mazur Theorem 1.3.11 (prime factorisation of Fredholm series over O[[T_1,…,T_m]], now on disk but its proof via Theorem 1.3.7 unread) for the identification of the components of Z_φ; these are needed for the 'components map onto Fredholm hypersurfaces' and Zariski-density clauses, not for equidimensionality. Dense classical points and unitary classicality require the application's actual overconvergent coefficient and control arguments (Chenevier §6.4.5 and §7 for unitary groups; Coleman–Mazur for the modular case). This packet does not infer them from eigenpacket-point classification.

gaps.title: Hida's control theorem for nearly ordinary Hilbert forms in weight μ + 2 > 2
gaps.detail: Skinner–Wiles Proposition 3.7 cites Hida, On nearly ordinary Hecke algebras for GL(2) over totally real fields, Adv. Stud. Pure Math. 17 (1989), 139–169, Corollary 2.5, without proof; that paper and Hida, Ann. of Math. 128 (1988), 295–384 ([H1]) were not obtained (Project Euclid refused automated access; the Annals is not open). The weight-two case is proved from the definitions (Skinner–Wiles p. 37). The higher-weight case needs a control statement comparing T_∞(U, 𝒪)/P_{μ,ψ,φ} with the weight-(μ + 2) nearly ordinary Hecke algebra; no other packet plans it.

gaps.title: Hida's control theorems for ordinary homology of X₁(Np^r)
gaps.detail: Emerton–Pollack–Weston use Hida, Galois representations into GL₂(ℤ_p[[X]]) attached to ordinary cusp forms, Invent. Math. 85 (1986), Theorem 3.1 ((lim→ H₁(Np^r; ℚ_p/ℤ_p)^ord)^Γ ≅ H₁(Np; ℚ_p/ℤ_p)^ord), and Hida, Modules of congruence of Hecke algebras and L-functions associated with cusp forms, Amer. J. Math. 110 (1988), Theorem 1.9 (M_m/ω_{r,k} ≅ (M_{r,k})_{m_{r,k}}). Neither paper is freely available and neither was read; the cohomological proof (Hida's ordinary part of group cohomology of Γ₁(Np^r) with a Shapiro/Λ-adic argument) should be planned here once a source is obtained (e.g. Hida's Elementary theory of L-functions, ch. 7).

gaps.title: Hida's and Wiles's constructions of the big Galois representation and its ordinary filtration (primary proofs unread)
gaps.detail: L4 plans Hida's big Galois representation T^ord, its nearly ordinary twist and its ordinary filtration from Ochiai (Ann. Inst. Fourier 55, 2005, §1) and Emerton–Pollack–Weston (§2.3), which quote Hida, Galois representations into GL₂(ℤ_p[[X]]) attached to ordinary cusp forms (Invent. Math. 85, 1986) and Wiles, On ordinary λ-adic representations associated to modular forms (Invent. Math. 94, 1988, Theorems 2.2.1–2.2.2). Neither is freely available and neither was read. The planned route (limits of ordinary parts of Tate modules of J₁(Np^t), Eichler–Shimura at weight two, Mazur–Wiles ordinarity, interpolation of determinants by IHG.4) is the standard one; its details are a gap until those papers are read.

gaps.title: Ochiai's two-variable Coleman map and the length formula
gaps.detail: Theorem B of Ochiai (2005) quotes Ochiai, A generalization of the Coleman map for Hida deformations (Amer. J. Math. 125, 2003, Theorem 3.14) for the map Ξ and the equality of lengths at height-one primes, and On the two-variable Iwasawa main conjecture (Compositio Math. 142, 2006) for its sequel. Neither is freely available and neither was read. L4 builds Ξ from Kings–Loeffler–Zerbes's big logarithm (Theorem 8.2.3), which is free; the identification of KLZ's map with Ochiai's, and the length formula (1) of L4/two-variable-l-function, remain to be checked against Ochiai 2003.

gaps.title: Nonordinary family inputs: Galois representations over the eigencurve, Liu's triangulation and Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao
gaps.detail: L4/coleman-family-regulator follows Loeffler–Zerbes, Rankin–Eisenstein classes in Coleman families (arXiv:1506.06703v2), §§4.6, 6.3–6.4, 7.1. It imports the Galois representation over a Coleman family (Theorem 4.6.6, via overconvergent étale cohomology), Liu's triangulation theorem (R. Liu, Triangulation of refined families, Comment. Math. Helv. 90, 2015), Andreatta–Iovita–Stevens's overconvergent Eichler–Shimura isomorphism and Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao's cohomology of families of (φ, Γ)-modules (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 27, 2014). None of these is planned by a roadmap below this one, and none was read beyond the statements quoted by Loeffler–Zerbes.

gaps.title: Weight-two cusp-form dimension input in Hida control
gaps.detail: Hida 1986 §5 (5.8), p.262, invokes Hida, Invent. Math. 79 (1985), Proposition 6.2 and Ribet [24] for the weight-two ordinary cusp-form dimension. Those primary proofs have not been read in this review. The p≥5 control statement is verified as a source statement, but this endpoint remains a prerequisite gap.

gaps.title: Raw family congruence module versus Hida free closures
gaps.detail: Hida (1986) (3.9), pp.252–253, uses free closures of the projected lattices. The raw annihilator congruence module need not equal that free-closure module unless the relevant projected lattices are reflexive. Establish the comparison map, its finite/pseudonull discrepancy, and explicit equality hypotheses before transferring Hida Theorem 3.6’s principal-annihilator conclusion to the raw module.

gaps.title: Global analytic coefficient chart cover and descent
gaps.detail: The later author §3.1.2, p.23, explicitly rejects full tensor-dual equality, and §3.1.4, p.26, constructs the tensor action by bounded multiplication. These local defects are repaired. The global eigenvariety still needs a cover by analytic coefficient charts and Banach symbol descent, including high-conductor and non-rational weights; nice neighbourhoods of classical integer weights alone are not an admissible cover of all weight space.

gaps.title: Banach symbol descent beyond nice classical charts
gaps.detail: The later author Lemma3.7 and Theorem3.10, pp.28–30, prove the closed-submodule and specialization claims on nice PID charts. Corollary3.12 has the E₂ exception (weight0, sign−, ν≥1), retained by the global-image convention. To instantiate the global machine on every weight chart, supply the corresponding Banach/compact restriction and specialization descent interfaces, including coefficient extensions; no arbitrary closed-kernel argument is a substitute.

gaps.title: Critical-slope paired zero-counting input
gaps.detail: The non-θ-critical case uses the paired-refinement Newton-polygon theorem attributed to Mazur and cited as Pollack Theorem3.3 in Bellaïche pp.38–39. The proof outline identifies this input but it is not a supplied node of the present prerequisites; it cannot be replaced by a general assertion about analytic functions of order k+1.

gaps.title: Galois representation normalization bridge
gaps.detail: Identify the EPW ordinary Hecke representation with Ochiai’s T^ord using the geometric Frobenius convention, contragredient and Tate twist, and check determinant and ordinary-line characters. Ochiai §1, pp.114–115 supplies the latter normalization but does not itself prove this bridge.

gaps.title: Family Selmer perfectness and arithmetic local comparisons
gaps.detail: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3 states derived control only when the actual local maps commute with derived base change, and its determinant target requires normality, perfectness and torsion cohomology. Prove these for the two-variable, possibly nonregular Hida branch; compute inertia/exceptional correction cones and the extended-to-classical Selmer comparison. The original direct-summand argument establishes none of these omitted conclusions.

gaps.title: KLZ–Ochiai regulator and integral period comparison
gaps.detail: Construct the normalization bridge from KLZ §8.2’s unramified regulator (with its H⁰ kernel and pole-residue term) to Ochiai’s Ξ and Theorem B height-one length formula. Prove the integral comparison of the resulting analytic periods with L1’s period module before claiming a branch-unit ratio. Agreement up to pointwise nonzero periods at a dense set does not prove a unit-valued analytic ratio.

gaps.title: Quaternionic ordinary finite generation on torsion characters
gaps.detail: Skinner–Wiles Proposition3.3, pp.35–36, uses constant-rank finite-level group-ring freeness, rejected by E11. The packet correctly replaces it by projectivity but its subsequent untwisted level-independence argument bounds only the trivial prime-to-p torsion-character component. Prove character-twisted control/uniform generator bounds on every factor and the completed-projective descent. Do not infer finite generation of the whole tower from its trivial-character coinvariants.

gaps.title: Parallel-weight Hilbert ordinary construction and semisimplicity
gaps.detail: DKV §3.1, pp.846–847, restates the parallel-weight Hida–Wiles finite-freeness/control input; Skinner–Wiles’s definite even-degree theorem alone does not cover it for arbitrary F. DKV p.857 credits reducedness at cond(χ)=𝔫 to Hida Theorem3.6 and Corollary3.7, pp.381–382. Supply that primary ordinary newform/control argument, including U_𝔭 and tame bad-prime semisimplicity; normality of good-prime Petersson operators alone does not prove reducedness of the full Hecke image.

gaps.title: Integral comparison of quotient and eigensymbol period conventions
gaps.detail: EPW Proposition4.1.4, pp.29–30, specializes an integral homology eigenquotient, whereas ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L1/integral-period-lattices is the saturated cohomological eigenline. Supply an integral Hecke-compatible perfect pairing/control comparison with dual or divided-power coefficients, prove torsion/congruence corrections and coefficient factorials are accounted for, and identify the dual line. Rational Eichler–Shimura and rank-one freeness alone do not identify these integral lattices up to a unit.

gaps.title: Integral branch degeneracy-map comparison
gaps.detail: EPW Theorem4.3.2 relies on the residual injectivity of Lemmas4.5.2–4.5.3 and Wiles’s ordinary Ihara input. R14.4 supplies degeneracy maps, not this residual injectivity theorem. Supply the precise non-Eisenstein ordinary level-raising exact sequence and full-Hecke-eigenvector vanishing statement before deducing the family integral isomorphism/unit period ratio.

gaps.title: Theta radius-change and finite-slope coefficient interface
gaps.detail: Bellaïche arXiv v1 p.26 fixes a radius r≤1, then p.27 states a raw exact sequence for D=D[r]. At r=1 bounded moments μ(1)=0, μ(z^n)=1 have an unbounded inverse under the transposed first derivative, so the sequence is not exact in D[1]. Use the global dagger radius-loss sequence and prove the finite-slope radius-link comparison to the locally analytic symbol model, including the determinant twist and U_p slope shift. Locally analytic piecewise polynomial kernels on radii<1 must also be distinguished from one global V_k.

gaps.title: Definite class set before quotient by the adelic centre
gaps.detail: R18.3/definite-class-set is D×\D_f×/(U A_f×), whereas Skinner–Wiles §3.2 uses D×\D_f×/U. Supply the finite-ray-class fibre comparison with the exact level units and global centre; centre-quotient finiteness alone does not prove the statement used here.

sourceIssues.locator: §3.2, Proposition 3.3 and its proof, pp. 35–36 (Numdam PDF pages 32–33)
sourceIssues.printed: The proposition concludes freeness of the ordinary direct summand with a rank computed from only the untwisted coinvariants.
sourceIssues.correction: Keep finite-level projectivity factor by factor. To pass to a completed projective module and deduce Λ′-freeness, prove uniform finite generation on every torsion-character factor (or all corresponding maximal ideals), not just the augmentation factor. The constant-rank claim across finite group-ring factors needs an additional argument and is not retained. The completed finite-generation/projectivity input is a packet gap.
sourceIssues.reason: The ordinary idempotent gives a projective summand at a finite level. A product of character-local rings permits different ranks. Moreover, a nontrivial prime-to-p character factor can have zero untwisted coinvariants while being nonzero, so untwisted compact Nakayama cannot prove the needed global finite generation.

sourceIssues.reason: Γ preserves the coefficients of a divisor, so the divisors n({0} − {∞}), n ≥ 1, lie in pairwise different Γ-orbits and Δ₀/Γ is infinite; moreover a modular symbol is additive, Φ(nδ) = nΦ(δ), so the values at orbit representatives are not independent and Φ ↦ (Φ(δ_i))_i is not onto a direct sum of invariants. The conclusions Bellaïche draws need the presentation of Δ₀ by Manin relations instead.

review.notes: Independent Codex review, session codex-otr40e. Checked all 121 target-level nodes, all 69 pinned baseline declarations, supplier contracts, current upstream/library ownership, API/tests/planets and all 18 source issues. Corrected source hypotheses, integral lattices, Banach/symbol specialization, spectral fibres, Galois twists and conditional Selmer/Hilbert inputs. The later Bellaïche author copy repairs several early-preprint defects but retains an exceptional E₂ quotient. Accepted as a complete target-level pass with 21 explicit proof/interface gaps and 15 supplier requests, not as a closed or formalized roadmap. L0a remains closed; the other seven layers are planned. Suggested Lean elaborates with 12 proof-placeholder warnings only; heavy missing carriers stay in the packet. The uneditable reader requires the exact updates listed in the review and handoff.
